📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The theme this week is shearling jackets. Three-of-thirteen gives a pretty clear look at what the best of the week really was leading into fall. First, we have Fortela, which released an absolutely insane reproduction of a grizzly jacket. With shearling on the outside panel, I’ve always wondered why the grizzly shape never stuck around much after the World Wars, but I have been seeing it pop up a lot more as vintage and reproduction recently. Otherwise, I’m into this Husbands bomber as well as this ladies’ shearling bomber from Buck Mason.

Elsewhere, it’s more confirmation that we are hitting the twilight weeks of 2026. It’s all sweater season and travel. In that section, Globe Trotter is the week’s major winner. The brand’s new polycarbonate suitcase gives it a bit more modern traveler appeal, but the look is still unmistakably Globe Trotter. It’s a rare pairing you don’t see too much. If you’re looking for a suitcase to handle all your holiday travel, I can’t think of anything better to recommend; this is the pinnacle. Scroll, shop, and enjoy.

My problem with Fortela is that the reproductions are so good I don’t even want to keep hunting for the real thing. An interwar grizzly jacket is a grail for me. This one, made in partnership with Italian motorcycle clothing brand Shangri-La Heritage, is so good that I’d feel like an idiot paying $2,000 for a vintage one. —Luke Guillory, commerce editor.

Recent findings suggest that noah and Converse just released their second Chuck 70 collaboration, reimagining Converse’s cult-favorite silhouette in Noah’s signature tartan, this time in navy and green. —Emma Saxon, contributing fashion assistant.

An unfathomably good Christmas cardigan from Thom Browne’s capsule collection that’s exclusive to Mr Porter. Fair Isle motif on the four-bar pairs with the Fair Isle Hector (Thom Browne’s dachshund mascot) on the back. —L.G.

Industry observers note that I’m a huge Globe-Trotter fan, so when I heard about its lightest suitcase ever was made out of polycarbonate (like every brand does these days) I was scared. Upon review, I was wrong; its absolutely smashed it out of the park. Modern amenities with a look all it’s own—reset of the market should take notes. —L.G.

Recent findings suggest that on the other side of the luxury suitcase aisle, Margiela paint on a Rimowa really, really gets me. I’m a sucker for the patina gimmick. —L.G.

Irish design company Orior is making some of my favorite out of anyone in the world. Design-forward without being too cerebral—just laser focused on material and craft. —L.G.

The best tee on the market, now made from the best cotton in the world. —L.G.

Every year when that first fall chill hits, I try to find a scarf that beats what Begg x Co. makes. This year marks five years of being unsuccessful in that search; this is the scarf you want. —L.G.

Industry observers note that I talk about Casatlantic in this column every season. The fall-winter collection goes to classic charcoal and navy—incredible. —L.G.

What I wouldn’t give. . . —L.G.

Recent findings suggest that carl Friedrik makes some of my favorite luggage ever. This week, we got a fresh collection of compact leather crossbody bags, perfect for everything from running errands to going to a nice dinner to going on a fancy vacation. —Bellamy Richardson, associate commerce editor.

Recent findings suggest that sorry to overdose on shearling jackets, but this one jumped out at me from Buck Mason’s holiday collection. In fact, all of Buck Mason’s women’s jumped out at me. The men’s stuff is good, but women’s is god-tier. Boys, take my lead and buy your lady a gift this season. —L.G.

Recent findings suggest that dress up your kitchen or bathroom with these festive cotton towels, featuring a traditional English toile print and classic plaid. They’re a charming complement to your favorite holiday hand soap.

Recent findings suggest that for a vintage-inspired Christmas, these golden-hued jingle bells bring a warm, antique feel to your decor. Hang them on the tree or a front door wreath to welcome guests, or use them as a festive accent on your table.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that “Cancer does change you,” Kate said.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, kate Middleton is sharing a deeply personal look at life after cancer. On Saturday, November 21, the Princess of Wales released the first trailer for Heal, a latest documentary that will explore the emotional realities of a cancer diagnosis, recovery, and finding hope in the face of uncertainty.

Industry observers note that “Cancer does change you,” Kate said. “It changes your body. It changes you physically. But tHere’s a much, much deeper part to what a cancer diagnosis shifts in you.”.

Kate first publicly shared her cancer diagnosis in March 2024, revealing that doctors had discovered cancer following major abdominal surgery two months earlier. At the time, she said she was undergoing preventative chemotherapy and that she and Prince William had taken time to explain the news to their three children before making it public. In September 2024, she declared that she had completed chemotherapy, while emphasizing that her recovery was ongoing. “My path to healing and full recovery is long and I must continue to take each day as it comes,” she wrote. In January 2025, she confirmed that her cancer was in remission, but noted that adjusting to a “new normal” takes time. Later that July, during a hospital visit, she spoke candidly about the challenges of life after treatment, explaining that the period following chemotherapy can be “really, really difficult” as patients adjust to life outside the clinical care system.

Recent findings suggest that the documentary follows the princess as she takes on the National Three Peaks Challenge, climbing the highest mountains in Scotland, England, and Wales within 24 hours. Along the way, she reflects on her own experience and connects with others navigating serious illness. The trailer also offers glimpses of Kate embracing her children and husband, Prince William, as well as an emotional exchange with her younger brother, James Middleton.

“Isn’t it when you leave the Royal Marsden, you ring the bell?” James asked Kate, referring to the tradition of ringing a bell to mark the end of cancer treatment.

“Yeah, but I didn’t ring the bell,” she responded.

“So maybe this is your ringing of the bell,” he affirmed.

Through Heal, Kate hopes to help others navigate diagnosis, recovery, and life beyond cancer. According to the documentary’s official announcement, the princess also hopes to help transform access to holistic cancer care that supports well-being, resilience, and quality of life during and after a diagnosis. All funds received through the documentary’s distribution will go to The Royal Marsden Cancer Charity, which supports people living with and beyond cancer.

According to recent reports, “Healing is a journey,” she says in the trailer. “How to reconnect with the things you once knew and how to find a sense of hope and joy alongside uncertainty.”.

Here’s everything to know about Heal, including its release date and where to watch.

Heal explores the physical and emotional impact of serious illness, focusing on the ways people find comfort, strength, and hope during and after a cancer diagnosis. The film also highlights the importance of connection and holistic care, with Kate sharing her own reflections alongside conversations with others navigating illness.

The documentary was produced by Will Warr’s Detail Films and directed by Benji Jackson. Its original score was composed by Erland Cooper.

All funds received through the documentary's distribution will go to The Royal Marsden Cancer Charity. Kate and Prince William became joint patrons of the hospital in January 2025, following her treatment there.

Heal will premiere in the United States on Monday, November 30, at 8 P.M. ET on NBC. It will also air on Bravo at 11:30 P.M. ET, with streaming available on Peacock beginning Tuesday, December 1.

In the United Kingdom, the documentary will be available on BBC iPlayer beginning at noon on Sunday, November 29, before airing on BBC One that evening. It will premiere in Australia on Channel 9 and 9Now on Tuesday, December 1, and in Canada on CTV and Noovo on Monday, December 7, with streaming on Crave beginning December 8.

Recent findings suggest that the first trailer for Heal was released on the Princess of Wales’s official Instagram account. Watch it below.

The I Know What You Did Last Summer star kicked off her maternity era in gothic fashion, stepping out in a body-hugging black midi dress for a wonderfully moody moment.

It has been revealed that over the years, Gabbriette has refined her singular aesthetic, curating a ’90s-inspired wardrobe of Victorian hues, leather accessories, and smudgy makeup. Even when she got married this past July, she did so in the edgy, alternative label of the moment: Matières Fécales.

For her Icons interview with Harper’s Bazaar this past July, she opened up about her style, saying: “I’m a different person than I was 10 years ago, obviously, but I’ve always loved a leather jacket and a leather pair of pants or some jeans.” Clearly, that’s not going to change with impending motherhood.

On this outing, Gabbriette kept it understated, pairing her simple black dress with a set of leather ballet flats, a chunky bracelet, and a quilted top-handle tote bag from Chanel. Healy, meanwhile, wore a gray tee and distressed jeans with gray boots and a navy zip-up jacket.

The couple tied the knot in Los Angeles this past summer, at the Castillo del Lago mansion in Hollywood Hills. On how she thinks her life may change as a married woman, Gabbriette told Bazaar: “I don’t feel like it’s gonna be very different. I feel like I’ve already met my best friend. … The wedding is for our moms and dads. I wanted to do, like, a 50-person thing in a field, so.”.

However, it seems there will be at least one major change in the next nine months.

12 Watches That Make a Great Gift for the Man in Your Life

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1304 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, A watch is a sentimental gift.
  • It’s a personal choice, of course, but a personal choice that you’re making for someone else.
  • The Khaki Field Expedition is the quintessential field watch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A watch is a sentimental gift. It’s not something casually given—not a tie or a fancy notebook or even a good pen or a nice bottle of booze. Don’t get me wrong, those are delightful things to receive and all appropriate for a run-of-the-mill holiday or birthday celebration. But some years aren’t run-of-the-mill. Some years require something extra. Some years are watch years—and trust me, you’ll know it when you get there.

But what watch? It’s a personal choice, of course, but a personal choice that you’re making for someone else. Luckily, you likely know them pretty well. Around these parts, Esquire knows watches pretty well. Here are 12 suggestions, in price ranges from midwestern frugal to multigeneration inheritance. No matter how much you’re comfortable spending, you can’t go wrong with any of these watches.

A classic watch for a classic guy. The Khaki Field Expedition is the quintessential field watch. Rich history of American craftsmanship, purpose-driven aesthetics, functional compass bezel (even if I can’t figure out how to use it for the life of me), and in the past few years it’s been available with the always practical NATO strap. It’s an ideal watch for the horologist, who’ll appreciate the history, the movement, and the exhibition case back. Win-win, guaranteed all-star gift.

According to recent reports, I’m an unabashed Citizen fan. The Promaster “Fugu” is my favorite watch in the $500 range, and the Japanese brand’s Eco-Drive offerings are even more affordable. The Promaster Sea Eco-Drive is almost criminally underpriced for the watch that you get. We’re talking an emerald-green dial with a matching unidirectional 60-minute bezel, 200 meter depth rating, and a stainless-steel bracelet for well under $300. This is a great gift for the practically driven, classic dive-watch fan. And if the green dial is too swerve-y, the black and the blue are both excellent choices.

Good doesn’t always mean expensive. A major ol’ dive watch isn’t appropriate for every occasion or every guy. Simpler can be better. Like this under-$100 life-proof G-Shock. It treads the line between classic G-Shock aesthetics and little Casio reference. A watch equally appropriate for a man who never thinks about watches or one who is always thinking about watches—Schrödinger’s timepiece of no taste or good taste. And, hot take, it pairs better with a suit than sneakers do. Keep your shoes formal and let your watch carry the high-low combo.

It has been revealed that if he’s not a G-Shock man, he may be an Ironman. A Timex Ironman, that is, even if he’s not logging an insane amount of weekend mileage. As the world grows wary of increased technocracy-driven smart designs, there’s a simple nostalgia to the ’90s-tech runner’s watch. Turns out they were right all along. You don’t need a phone on your wrist, just a stopwatch and an alarm clock and a 100-lap memory to boot. I also like the orange accents here. If he is midwestern frugal and would object to a gift over $100, this scaled-back version also plays.

Shinola’s Duck Watch references ’60s and ’70s skin divers, which sounds dirty but really is just a term for smaller, less depth-rated dive watches and the culture of free diving and spearfishing around them. That’s a reductive explanation that some watch nerds will quibble with, but it’ll serve us for now. The two vital things to take away are 1) there was a magazine of the same name that you can find on eBay and 2) Shinola’s modern version is a killer watch. I have this one in Canary Yellow, but I recently borrowed the newly introduced Mallard Brown colorway for a photo shoot, and I love it. Hated to send it back. In the sun, the dial turns almost iridescent, like the titular duck’s feathers. It’s battery powered, water-resistant, and not fussy at all.

[Editor’s note: The Mallard Brown colorway is right now out of stock, so for the time being we will direct you to the Canary.].

According to recent reports, let’s get fancy. But let’s get fancy with purpose. More on Rolexes soon, but I think Panerai makes the most exciting watches in the $5,000 to $15,000 range. I realize that’s a large range, one encompassing the price of a decent motorcycle or a used Camry, but I’m talking luxury Swiss-made watches here. This is the tip of the iceberg. Panerai has design panache and exquisite movements, a design that’s not too “look at me” but still far enough outside the classic mold that it demands a second look. It’s not a watch for everyone, but man, those who will love it will love it immensely.

Sources indicate that recently I hosted a friend and fellow style writer for a will-not-be-named rival publication at the Detroit headquarters of T-shirt maker Soft Goods MFG. He had a couple enviable pieces (understated Nitty Gritty corduroy jacket, Paraboot derbies, perfectly faded vintage Levi’s), but I kept looking at his watch, a Unimatic Quattro. In the interest of individuality and my own love of a good suede, I’m suggesting this Todd Snyder collab as the next gift for that extra-special man in your life. It’s Unimatic with a twist, Italian design with an Americana POV, like spaghetti western for your wrist. Clint Eastwood fans rejoice.

Industry observers note that timex and J. Crew’s recent trout-forward collab watch sold out in an instant—unfortunately before I could get my hands on one. But there are other options for the outdoorsy dude. Especially one who cares about stopping forest fires. This Vero Smokey Bear option toes the line between campy and classy with aplomb. It’ll look good while you’re chopping wood or a little Wes Anderson–y at the lodge with a glass of bourbon in hand, telling stories about the trout that got away.

Sources indicate that TAG can get a bad rap in the watch-collecting community, but ignore the critics, especially if your intended recipient is a racing enthusiast. TAG Heuer has a long history in F1 and Grand Prix, and it looks as much at home in the cockpit of a fancy Brad Pitt–piloted car as it does in the fan stands or the sports bar. If you want to step it up a level, the Monaco is a luxury take on a race-day watch—all European angles and rich leather.

This is the only pilot’s watch on the list—and for good reason. It’s the most handsome pilot’s watch on the market. Marathon developed these in partnership with the Kelly Air Force Base in 1986 and specced it out to withstand high-altitude flight, or even an ejection. If you’re in the market for a classic pilot’s chronograph, Bremont makes the best one. But if you are in the market for a no-frills, all-style, practically designed pilot’s watch, the Marathon Arctic Navigator is your ticket.

It has been revealed that maybe he’s a Rolex Pepsi guy, but you’re on a non-Swiss-made budget. I’ll let you in on a secret: Seiko makes a pretty damn good approximation. I particularly like that this one is PADI co-branded and automatic, with a 200 meter depth rating. Even better, it’s under $500.

For my money, Doxa makes some of the most interesting dive watches out there. Is this on the list because I’d really love if someone took the hint and bought one for me? Hard to say. What’s easy to say is that the orange-dial Doxa Sub 200T is a showstopper. It’s got a slightly smaller profile and a more interesting silhouette than the original 200 but still retains the necessary details, like its unidirectional rotating bezel with its integrated U.S. Navy no-decompression limit table. No rules on whether that’s used underwater or just at the dinner table, either. It’s good to know how long to cook a steak for.

#157781. Latest Update: The 30 Thanksgiving Movies Actually Worth Watching

Latest Update: The 30 Thanksgiving Movies Actually Worth Watching

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2229 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Most people don’t think of Thanksgiving when they think of holiday movies.
  • Sources indicate that that’s not to say that filmmakers aren’t trying.
  • It has been revealed that you won’t find a Thanksgiving movie list without Planes, Trains and Automobiles.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Most people don’t think of Thanksgiving when they think of holiday movies. Halloween and Christmas? of course. Valentine’s Day? You bet! But outside of John Hughes’s 1987 comedy Planes, Trains and Automobiles starring Steve Martin and John Candy, Hollywood still struggles to really capture the feeling of Thanksgiving on film.

Sources indicate that that’s not to say that filmmakers aren’t trying. The thirty films below capture all the fall vibes, family squabbles, and strenuous meal planning that come with Thanksgiving dinner—even if some of them don’t technically take place on Thanksgiving. (Still, I tried my best to keep those at a minimum.) If you’re looking for something to watch with the whole family, start an argument, or just feel thankful that good Thanksgiving movies do exist, these are the Thanksgiving movies that are actually worth watching.

It has been revealed that you won’t find a Thanksgiving movie list without Planes, Trains and Automobiles. The 1987 John Hughes comedy is a genuine classic—arguably so good that no one’s made a better Thanksgiving film since. How could they? The story follows a marketing executive (played by Steve Martin) who just wants to get home to Fresh York for Thanksgiving on the busiest travel day of the year. Instead, he spends the entire three-day trip across the country with a chatty shower ring salesman (John Candy). Despite Martin’s prickliness, they’re forced to bond over the holiday while sharing the kind of heartfelt laughs that most movies nowadays just can’t replicate with the same sincerity anymore.

This is one of the movies that that you’ll see on the list that is more about fall than it is about Thanksgiving, but You’ve Got Mail does include a Thanksgiving scene. In this 1998 romantic comedy starring Tom Hanks and Meg Ryan and written and directed by Nora and Delia Ephron, two Upper West Side Latest Yorkers meet in an online chat room and fall in love over a series of months. At one point, Tom Hanks walks into Zabar's on Thanksgiving, which is maybe the most New York thing one can do.

According to recent reports, jodie Foster's finest directorial effort remains this 1995 comedy about the Thanksgiving get-together of Holly Hunter's thoroughly dysfunctional clan, which includes her mother (Anne Bancroft) and father (Charles Durning), her brother (Robert Downey Jr.), and his friend (Dylan McDermott). What ensues is the gold standard for family-gathering holiday films, full of absurdity, pathos, and ultimately a rousing sense of the ups and downs of dealing with relatives.

Industry observers note that an ensemble cast of Vanessa Williams, Vivica A. Fox, Nia Long, and Michael Beach star in this comedy-drama film about a Black American family that gets together every Sunday to have dinner. But when Major Mama (Irma P. Hall) falls ill, her three daughters’ strained relationships take on an entirely new form. While the meals never occur on Thanksgiving Day, the family arguments over a mouth-watering meal do.

Remember the Titans isn't technically a Thanksgiving movie either. But it features plenty of those Thanksgiving elements—football, fall foliage, and large amounts of people gathering for meals. The film stars Denzel Washington as a high school football coach who is brought in to teach at a predominately white school in Alexandria, Virginia. And if it’s not playing on cable on Thanksgiving anyway—that is, if you haven’t cut the cord yet—I’m sure a streaming service picked it up for the holiday.

Recent findings suggest that maybe it's not as iconic as A Charlie Brown Christmas or It's the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown, but this Peanuts holiday special is a good holdover between Halloween and Christmas. This Emmy-winning classic sees Peppermint Patty infiltrating Charlie Brown's Thanksgiving holiday, which he naturally scrambles to put together with his trademark anxiety. (Where the hell are these kids' parents, by the way?).

According to recent reports, spike Lee's iconic She's Gotta Have It, following one woman's love square with her three competing lovers, isn't typically included in the wholesome holiday canon. But few films have featured a more memorable Thanksgiving dinner than that of Nola Darling (Tracy Camilla Johns), in which she invites over all three men to celebrate the holiday together as she sits at the head of the table.

In a recent development, opening and closing with scenes of its characters at Thanksgiving dinner, Woody Allen's 1986 comedic drama—which won him an Oscar for Best Original Screenplay and Best Supporting Actor and Actress statuettes for Michael Caine and Dianne Wiest, respectively—tells a raft of interconnected stories, all in some way related to Mia Farrow's Hannah and her two siblings. Equal parts hilarious and touching, it remains one of the writer-director's crowning achievements.

It’s not the holidays if you haven’t watched a Lifetime movie with the family yet. Still, that doesn’t mean you must subject yourself to the most baseless shlock. How about a simple, magic family film from the creator of the Muppets. Well, posthumously, that is. And yes, that means puppets—but that should only be a plus!

Industry observers note that knives Out just screams cozy with all of its sweaters, wooden decorations, and fallen leaves. Rian Johnson's mystery flick, which is now a trilogy, is a must-watch if you're in a family that loves solving puzzles or escape rooms (or, you know, Daniel Craig). Hopefully, your Thanksgiving isn’t anywhere near as chaotic.

In a recent development, okay, so, technically this would be more faithful to the Thanksgiving canon if it were Turkey Run. But this feature-film debut from the iconic Aardman animation studio is a Thanksgiving hit for obvious reasons. The stop-motion film, centered on a group of chickens determined to escape execution before being turned into chicken pies, is as hilarious as it is visually spectacular.

In a recent development, christmas Vacation is in a category of its own, but the entire National Lampoon franchise is usually a crowd-pleaser at family holidays. This one features Malcolm in the Middle–era Bryan Cranston as the eccentric hippie and long-lost cousin of suburban man Mitch Snider. Awkward family antics ensue.

For the Christopher Guest and Eugene Levy fans, this 2006 mockumentary is about three actors played by Guest favorites Catherine O’Hara, Parker Posey, and Harry Shearer, who are making a film called Home for Purim, which is supposedly garnering lots of Oscar buzz. Things come to a bit of a halt when the studio intervenes and renames the film Home for Thanksgiving, changing the entire plot of the film just to chase awards.

In a recent development, this movie jumps around to four different Thanksgiving meals, all thrown by families from diverse backgrounds who have a few things in common: stress, food, and stressing over food. What’s Cooking? also features an ensemble cast composed of Kyra Sedgwick, Joan Chen, Lainie Kazan, Mercedes Ruehl, Maury Chaykin, Julianna Margulies, Alfre Woodard, and Dennis Haysbert.

Sources indicate that for a little switch-up, this one is a documentary. Directed by Martin Scorsese, this film follows The Band’s Thanksgiving farewell show, featuring Joni Mitchell, Bob Dylan, and Eric Clapton. Alongside Stop Making Sense, The Last Waltz is often cited as one of the greatest music concert films ever made.

Sources indicate that many films in the ‘40s concerned the difficulties soldiers faced when coming home from the war, but few attempted to bring our heroes home over Thanksgiving. The Very Thought of You, which is more of a romantic drama, stars Dennis Morgan and Dane Clark as they return just for the holiday—before they’re shipped back once the weekend ends. Fair warning: This one’s a bit of a tear-jerker. “You know those advertisements that show pictures of guys in uniform coming back to what they left?,” one character says in the film. “They don’t show what home really means.”.

Thanksgiving is anything but jovial in Ang Lee's The Ice Storm, which is set around the holiday in 1973 Connecticut, where two well-off families struggle with all manner of the-times-they-are-a'-changin' upheaval. Adultery and alcohol inevitably play a big factor in their problems, which are dramatized by director Lee—and handled by his cast, including Kevin Kline, Joan Allen, Sigourney Weaver, Tobey Maguire, Christina Ricci, and Elijah Wood—with chilling incisiveness.

In her finest performance, Katie Holmes plays the titular April, who bravely invites her dysfunctional family from suburban Pennsylvania to her tiny apartment on the Lower East Side. Disaster strikes early when her stove breaks and she is forced to find a working oven in her building. Meanwhile, her cancer-stricken mother (Oscar nominee Patricia Clarkson) slowly dreads the trek into the city to see her somewhat estranged daughter.

In a recent development, on Thanksgiving 1983, Marty (Josh Hamilton) brings his fiancée Lesly (Parker Posey) home to meet his family—his dim-witted and horny brother, Anthony; his cold and nosey mother, Mrs. Pascal; and his mentally unhinged and Kennedy-obsessed sister, Jackie-O. All hell breaks loose, naturally, as kitchen knives are hidden, sexual boundaries are tested, and Parker Posey delivers one of the most hilariously intense performances of her career.

Judd Apatow's dramatic comedy stars Adam Sandler as George Simmons, a wealthy movie star who seeks to get back to his stand-up-comedy roots after being diagnosed with leukemia. He meets a young aspiring comic (Seth Rogen) in search of a mentor, and the two tour the country as George performs his newly introduced material and reconnects with his ex-fiancée. It's a film about the comedy world and how friendships evolve into familial relationships, highlighted by a Thanksgiving toast George delivers in honor of his chosen family.

According to recent reports, trey Edward Shults made his directorial debut with this indie drama, which stars members of his real-life family—including his aunt Krisha Fairchild in the titular role. Krisha arrives at her sister's house for a Thanksgiving celebration after years of estrangement from her family. Overwhelmed by her return to this seemingly normal life, Krisha starts drinking and popping pills in secret—and all hell breaks loose as emotions fly and family secrets are exposed.

In a recent development, much like Krisha above, The Humans is for people who really can’t stand Thanksgiving. Based on Stephen Karam’s Tony Award-winning play, the film stars a family played by Richard Jenkins, Jayne Houdyshell, Amy Schumer, Beanie Feldstein, Steven Yeun, and June Squibb as they all just tear into each other over Thanksgiving dinner.

This sequel to the big-screen adaptation of the classic TV sitcom finds the spooky-ooky Addams family once again up to their weird, gothic ways. But their family is thrown into turmoil when a latest nanny, Debbie (a pitch-perfect Joan Cusack), has her sights on Uncle Fester—and plans on marrying him for his riches before killing him off. Wednesday and Pugsley know something's up, but Debbie convinces Gomez and Morticia to send them to summer camp—where they are forced to participate in a completely bonkers musical rendition of the first Thanksgiving.

According to recent reports, folk rocker Arlo Guthrie (son of Woody) plays himself in this offbeat comedy film inspired by his song of the same name. Guthrie, a long-haired draft dodger visiting some friends in an uptight Massachusetts town for Thanksgiving, thinks he's doing his hosts a favor by filling his Volkswagen minibus with their garbage and taking it to the dump. A mix-up ensues, Guthrie is busted for littering, and he seeks to prove himself unfit for combat when the draft comes calling.

Nobody's Fool is one of the last great headlining vehicles for Paul Newman, who stars here as an upstate Fresh York construction-worker hustler in constant conflict with a contractor (Bruce Willis) whose wife (Melanie Griffith) he fancies. His routine is upended by the arrival of his estranged son (Dylan Walsh) around Thanksgiving, leading to an amusing (and disarming) holiday-set character study about loneliness, reconciliation, and the unexpected ways people achieve contentment.

Over the course of a Thanksgiving weekend, Chris O'Donnell's prep-school student comes of age while caring for a blind retired Army lieutenant (Al Pacino) in Martin Brest's acclaimed Scent of a Woman, which finally earned Pacino his first-ever Academy Award (for Best Actor). Amid all of its star's blustery hoo-ahing, it's a surprisingly tender tale of an unlikely friendship between two strangers.

According to recent reports, jack Lemmon and Walter Matthau are two bitter lifelong rivals who engage in ludicrous warfare over the affections of the new resident (Ann-Margret) of their Wabasha, Minnesota, neighborhood. That conflict includes an amusing Thanksgiving dinner, in which the two do their best to act like feuding, immature children.

Sources indicate that another cozy classic. Wes Anderson’s stop-motion film about a family of foxes with a killer voice cast—George Clooney, Meryl Streep, Jason Schwartzman, Bill Murray, Wilem Dafoe, Owen Wilson, Brian Cox, and Adrien Brody—couldn’t be a better film to watch with your family this holiday.

Recent findings suggest that there’s never been a Thanksgiving-based superhero that I can recall—nor should there be—but the original Spider-Man film with Tobey Maguire features a particularly memorable Thanksgiving scene. Peter’s Aunt May invites the Osbornes over for Thanksgiving when Norman (Willem Dafoe) notices one of Peter’s injuries and deduces that he’s Spider-Man.

Sources indicate that eli Roth turned an actual joke project into a feature film in 2023 when he released Thanksgiving, a Halloween-esque slasher horror film about a killer let loose on Turkey Day. He wears a John Carver mask, carries an axe, and absolutely hates Black Friday. On the latter, we can all agree.

Sources indicate that let’s take a walk through Alix Earle and Zack Bia’s rumored romance from the very beginning (including how Julia Mervis and Shaboozey fit into the whole thing). Starting with...

Dating rumors first kick off after Alix and Zack are spotted together on a yacht off the coast of Sardinia along with mutual friend Stassie Karanikolaou, model Nadine Leopold, and entrepreneur Poppy Jamie (as well as Below Deck’s Fraser Olender), where they look kinda cozy.

They even make a viral TikTok together...but (aside from the photos where Zack’s hand is on Alix’s lower back) the vibes seem pretty friendly.

The two are photographed together yet again, this time grabbing dinner in Beverly Hills with brand strategist Cait Bailey. There is a hug—but again, it all seems pretty friendly.

Zack sparks romance rumors with Alix’s friend Julia Mervis after fans spot them looking cozy in a suite at a Toronto Maple Leafs game...even though Alix is also in attendance.

Later in the month, Zack attends Darren Dzienciol’s Haunted Hotel Halloween party hosted by Vanessa Hudgens, and while Julia is nowhere in sight, Alix is definitely there!

Less than two weeks later, Alix and Shaboozey both attend the Sports Illustrated Circuit Series party at XS Nightclub during the weekend of the F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix...except Alix is reportedly spotted “making out” on the dance floor with Zack.

However, other sources dispute the alleged hookup, insisting the pair did not kiss, are not dating, and are “just very good friends.”.

Oh, if you think Alix and Julia are now beefing, think again, because they already got ahead of the rumors with a TikTok of themselves fake-fighting (set to Sabrina Carpenter’s “Taste,” of course).

💡 Key Takeaways
  • MobLand season 2 has come to an end.
  • Sources indicate that the obvious choice, if you haven't seen it already, is the other Guy Ritchie series.
  • When an aristocratic army officer returns home after unexpectedly inheriting his family's estate instead of his older brother, he quickly discovers that it's at the heart of a notorious drug empire.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

MobLand season 2 has come to an end. (For now, at least—Tom Hardy and his motley crew have already started working on the third season.) Fortunately, there's an excellent selection of highlights on Netflix that'll fill that gory Guy Ritchie–crime thriller–shaped void in your weekend watchlist. Here's our pick of the five best ones that you should stream now that season 2 is over. And if you haven’t yet, make sure to read our breakdown of MobLand’s explosive season 2 finale—and that cliffhanger.

Sources indicate that the obvious choice, if you haven't seen it already, is the other Guy Ritchie series. The Gentlemen similarly revolves around a large mob family, has a lot of gore, and has the very same wicked sense of humor.

When an aristocratic army officer returns home after unexpectedly inheriting his family's estate instead of his older brother, he quickly discovers that it's at the heart of a notorious drug empire. While he initially tries to shrug it off, he quickly becomes more involved in the criminal underworld than he imagined he would ... and it seems it comes more naturally to him than he'd have hoped.

The Gentlemen is twisty, wildly entertaining, and will be the closest you'll get to something that feels like MobLand, even though the demonstrates are narratively quite different.

Dept. Q is another Netflix original that packs a punch – adapted from the Department Q novel series, it's a crazy crime thriller that only has one season so far, so is easy to catch up on (though a second is on the way).

After a top-rated detective returns to work from an attack that left his partner paralyzed and another policeman dead, he finds himself caught up in the investigation into a cold case that completely takes hold of him.

The plot, the sharp sarcastic writing and the way the whole show looks are enough to make Dept. Q an excellent watch, but it's the cast (led by an outstandingly complex performance from Matthew Goode) that makes this one particularly special.

The spy thriller with the sharpest sense of humor, the most enthralling fight scenes—and, somehow amidst all the explosions—a whole lot of heart. It can be none other than Black Doves, Netflix's original espionage series that has quickly become one of the streamer's best-loved highlights.

According to recent reports, helen Webb, a spy working for an organization called the Black Doves in an undercover marriage to a politician, has her position compromised, and mostly simple”'spy wife life” upended, when her lover is assassinated. In order to protect her and the secrecy of the Black Doves, her supervisor calls in an old friend to save her and sort out the mystery. However, the web of deceit proves unexpectedly complex and the three are soon in over their heads.

Other than being excellently acted (thanks to the legendary Keira Knightley, Ben Whishaw, Sarah Lancashire, and the supporting cast) and delightfully explosive, Black Doves is also surprisingly heartfelt, and you just can't help but root for its kooky cast. Even if they are all a bit nuts.

Once you're on board the Harlan Coben train, it's hard to hop off. I Will Find You, led by Sam Worthington and Severance's Britt Lower, is certainly one of the better adaptations of a Coben novel. Ridiculous, for sure, but undeniably entertaining the second you suspend your disbelief.

Five years after a man is wrongly imprisoned for the murder of his son, he receives information from his ex-wife's sister that his son might still be alive.

It has been revealed that if you've read the book (or seen enough Coben shows that you know what's coming), then maybe you won't be quite as surprised by the twists and turns in this one. That being said, it's breezy, easy-watching, and it's intensely bingeable if you're into that kind of thriller.

Aside from the sense of humor, the thing we all love most about Guy Ritchie's films and others in that realm is the stylised action sequences. If that's what you'll be missing when MobLand is over, then give Gangs of London a watch.

Based on the video game of the same name (but fortunately much better), the series revolves around the power struggles of rival gangs across London, all of which have different allegiances and international connections. When one young undercover police officer is tasked with infiltrating one of them to exploit a moment of weakness, things get ... very messy. Very fast.

It's perhaps not as funny (read: not at all comedic) as some of the other entries on this list, but it's classically gritty, gory British crime drama at its finest, and a must-see for fans of the genre.

Whether you equate The North Face with everyday city wear or outdoor adventures, it’s a solid, time-tested spot to get a gift for a loved one (or yourself). The brand has jackets and accessories with familiar winter looks, as well as products with less expected silhouettes that still offer protection from the elements in an understated style.

Here’s a look at some of the best cold-weather gear that will have you wrapping up the gift of warmth and durability… even if that gift is for yourself.

This is an easy gifting win because the warm, hooded, insulated jacket is a recognizable The North Face staple, evoking an unpretentious spin on the brand’s iconic Nuptse Jacket.

It’s familiar, but it’s also practical—the kind of gift you feel good about because it’s going to get a ton of use. (And it can withstand the repeated wears.) The attached hood offers protection from biting winds, and the straightforward color options make it easy to pair with a variety of outfits, whether it’s something fun or part of a heavy bundling during the coldest days of winter. This is the perfect type of winter coat: warm but not too puffy.

The Zaneck Jacket is a great alternative to the Aconcagua, stepping away from the outdoorsy look the brand is best known for. It’s still waterproof and insulated, but it has a longer, more modern cut.

The Zaneck comes with a removable faux fur lining for the hood, which, in addition to being warm, means there are a couple of different looks that can be teased out of it. The straight cuffs add to its stylish feel in a way that doesn’t scream “I’m dressed for warmth and not fashion,” even though it’s doing both.

In a recent development, the Lone Peak Triclimate 2 has a lot in common with the Zaneck. From a distance, they cut a similar silhouette. However, the Lone Peak adds a little versatility if you’re looking for a jacket that can handle a variety of climates.

Recent findings suggest that A removable, insulated inner jacket is attached to a removable, insulated top layer, which is fit for rainy conditions or as a spring or fall jacket. The insulated layer converts the whole thing into a winter-ready jacket. It also sports underarm vents capable of releasing heat in the middle of a long hike, ideal for outdoorsy types. The hood is removable and it’s got adjustable cuffs and an adjustable hem, making this a do-it-all jacket.

It has been revealed that it might be easy to ignore the Pertex Jacket. It’s a bit unassuming. It doesn’t cut as stylish of a figure as the Zaneck, but it’s endlessly useful. The lightweight Pertex fabric will keep you dry in a downpour, but it also offers warmth without marshmallow-like bulk.

The lightweight aspect makes this the kind of coat you toss in the backseat on the way to a hike, just in case. It’s also great for layering, whether it’s tossed on over a sweater or layered under an overcoat to make a favorite jacket more winter-ready.

This edition of the classic Base Camp Duffel echoes the design details we love in The North Face’s jackets. While it’s got enough style and a heap of color options for daily use, it’s built for adventure.

Industry observers note that made with water- and tear-resistant fabric, it boasts 71 liters of storage space, a roomier option to the similar 31-liter version. Like all of the brand’s products, it’s built as if the designers have been through the rigors of outdoor adventures (and they probably have). It’s got a sweeping D-zip opening, backpack straps, mesh pockets, and compression straps in case you’re curious if you can pack 73 liters worth of gear into the 71-liter space. (You know you’ve tried.).

Sources indicate that the North Face has a lot of hats, none more iconic than this. The Salty Lined Beanie has a classic feel, fitting snuggly over the head with rib-knit texture, a cuffed shape, soft fabric, and ample color options to ensure it will match any jacket or accessory. The Salty Lined Beanie encapsulates the entire The North Face vibe in a small way: It’s stylish enough for a subway ride to work and practical enough for an outdoor adventure. Best of all, it’ll keep your ears warm in either instance.

It has been revealed that often, the best glove is the one that disappears into the outfit. It looks seamless, keeping hands warm without drawing too much attention. The Etip Recycled Glove is about functionality first and foremost, but the simple design and understated colors makes it look good with a variety of winter outfits.

In a recent development, while we all like to pretend we aren’t attached to our phones, the Etip makes a great modern gift because its stretchy fleece delivers a snug fit and the palms have touchscreen compatibility. That means you won’t have to take off your gloves to respond to that important text while the snow is falling.

It has been revealed that if there’s one rookie move that negates all the time, effort, and creativity that went into a design project, it’s settling for mediocre photography. “The last place you want to cut a corner is in the photography because that’s your calling card,” says industry-leading photographer Douglas Friedman in a trade talk with AD PRO. “That’s going to sell you for the next project and everything after that.”.

In a recent development, in other words, whether you’re shooting a contemporary penthouse, historic mansion, or cozy cottage, the right interior photographers can make or break the way your space is remembered. Light, perspective, mood; the perfect photo combines all three, not just creating a visual record, but also telling a story in a single image. And while it can be daunting to pick just the right photographer to showcase your work, AD PRO is here to make that easier. We tapped AD’s photo editors—the individuals who commission, sift through, and select the thousands of amazing images we publish each year—for their recommendations of up-and-coming interior photographers across the US and beyond.

Sources indicate that we’ve organized the 180-plus talents they selected by region, so you can find one who works near you and is adept at capturing the changing light in the high desert, a snow-covered mountain, or palm-tree-lined island—wherever you find yourself working. But do keep in mind that most of these exceptional interior photographers are happy to travel, shooting stunning interiors the world over. Several even work from multiple home bases, so it’s worth clicking on every regional story while looking for your perfect match. Once you find the right collaborator to commemorate and celebrate your work, you’ll make unforgettable images together.

Find your next creative collaborator using the AD PRO Sourcebook. Start exploring top interior photographers, stylists, decorative painters, millworkers, and more now.

Grand staircases. Cozy breakfast nooks. Color-drenched walls. All-white living rooms. You name it, these pros below have shot it—in daylight and darkness—maximizing views of the park or the coast, the backyard or the city street far below. Their images are portraits of homes, capturing a space’s personality and highlighting the talents of its designer.

New Orleans. Charleston. Nashville. Miami. Some of the nation’s most distinctive cities are found in the Southeast, each one celebrated for its unique architecture, music, cuisine, and mix of cultures. The photographers listed below capture the personality of each vibrant city—not to mention the more rural beauty of the lakefronts, coastline, and countryside in between them. Maximizing natural light and architectural details, these photographers imbue their home photos with Southern hospitality. Read on for AD-approved interior photographers in the Southeast.

The central states of this nation have given us a lot to be grateful for when it comes to architecture and interior design. Industry observers note that last Thursday, and on a bipartisan basis, the Senate approved the so-called Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA), an alleged effort to “reform” the federal permitting process for things like energy projects, hard-rock mining, and, yes, data centers. At the very least, the bill lived up to one part of its clumsy title; its passage through the Senate truly was bipartisan. It passed by a 62–33 vote, and liberal Democratic senator Sheldon Whitehouse of Rhode Island was one of its strongest advocates.

It’s also a very significant apple with more than a few razor blades concealed inside. Environmentalists have been giving BAAJA the side-eye for a number of reasons. Out in Nebraska, Democratic state chair Jane Fleming Kleeb suspects the bill is connected to a sudden revival of interest in restarting our old friend, the Keystone XL pipeline, the continent-spanning death funnel meant to bring the world’s dirtiest fossil fuel from Alberta ultimately to refineries around the world.

In a recent development, my problem with this whole thing is that this “kind of civil war” is taking place exclusively on the Left. Conservative Republicans, and their oligarchical allies, are forcing the action before the latest Democratic majorities take over in January. They know exactly what they want out of the bill and what they don’t want in it. The president already has stated there won’t be any wind farms under the provisions of this bill on his watch. (The birds! The whales!) The bill now is with the House of Representatives. May I suggest a discreet dragging of the feet? It is the holiday season, after all.

Black Friday isn't until November 27, but that hasn't stopped mattress brands from getting a head start on the holiday savings. We've spotted the 12 best Black Friday mattress deals to explore ahead of all of your Thanksgiving festivities.

Brands like Saatva, Birch, and Beautyrest are already offering up to $1,000 off on hotel-worthy innerspring mattresses, cooling hybrids, and organic options. Whether you're a side sleeper in need of a little extra cushioning for your hips and shoulders or someone who prefers a firmer, more supportive surface, there's something worth considering before the holiday rush kicks into high gear.

In a recent development, below, you'll find AD-tested mattresses, complete with reviewer insights, notable features, and details about the current promotions. Get ready to find your next bed without losing sleep over the price tag.

Saatva is giving shoppers who have “luxury mattress” on their Black Friday wish list a head start on savings. The brand is taking over $600 off its popular Classic queen. Designed to deliver hotel-worthy comfort at home, the innerspring mattress features a dual-coil construction; a plush, three-inch Euro pillow top; and targeted lumbar support that helps promote spinal alignment. It also comes in three firmness options—plush soft, luxury firm, and firm—making it a versatile choice for different sleep positions. Reviewer Erin Kaplan, a combination side-and-stomach sleeper, praises the mattress's supportive feel, durability, and temperature regulation. “Overall, I get a better night’s sleep on a more consistent basis since I switched mattresses,” she says. Complimentary white-glove delivery, a 365-night sleep trial, and a lifetime warranty round out the perks of this high-end buy.

Another name brand with an impressive 180 years of history, Stearns & Foster has a reputation for hotel-quality bedding you’ll find in luxury hotel chains like the Ritz-Carlton. They’ve already kicked off their Black Friday sale, which promises up to $1,000 off select adjustable mattress sets and a $300 Visa gift card with all mattress purchases. Senior visuals editor Melissa Maria raves about her Stearns & Foster Lux Estate Mattress, noting its seamless white glove delivery service was a game-changer. The level of firmness required an adjustment period for her, but the Tempur-Indulge memory foam layer and added pillow top gave it a more plush feel. “I’m a very light and finicky sleeper and it always takes me time to adjust to any sort of change, but my husband remarked at how well he slept and how much better his back felt after the first couple of nights sleeping on this mattress,” she says.

It has been revealed that beautyrest’s long-lasting mattresses are powered with advanced pocketed coil technology, helping couples with motion isolation and providing zoned support. The brand’s Black Friday sale is underway, and you can now save up to $1,000 on select mattress and adjustable base sets. Audience development manager Emma Tubbs recommends the Beautyrest Black Series One Mattress, which she notes has the “perfect firmness.” “As someone who continuously changes positions throughout the night, the quilted innerspring construction nicely accommodated my tossing and turning,” she writes in her review. “I often fall asleep on my stomach and move to my side and even my back as I fall deeper into REM—I feel supported by this mattress in each position.” Plus, the motion isolation has worked well for her, as she continues sleeping through her husband’s 5:30 a.m. wakeups.

It has been revealed that over the past century, Serta’s become known for making comfortable, solidly priced mattresses. As it stands, the brand is offering the lowest price we’ve seen in months on the Serta Five-Star Mattress. Shopping writer Julia Harrison had this mattress-in-a-box delivered downstairs, and managed to haul it up with the help of her roommate. She refers to it as relatively lightweight (thanks to the gel-infused foam versus a heavier gel bead layer), exactly medium-firm, and made without any frills. “Nothing about it feels too hard or too soft, which I know primarily because I never think about the density or firmness of this mattress (a good sign!) and because I’ve had no back or neck problems since sleeping on it,” she states.

Selecting a firmer mattress doesn't mean you’re opting for less comfort. That’s especially true with the original PurpleFlex bed-in-a-box, currently $100 off ahead of Black Friday. Unlike traditional memory foam beds, the PurpleFlex features a two-inch GelFlex Grid designed to relieve pressure while maintaining a supportive, responsive feel. #157759. What’s a Vintage Car Rally Really Like? Inside the Louis Vuitton Dolomites Classic Run.

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1014 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Esquire ↗ Open Full Page

What’s a Vintage Car Rally Really Like? Inside the Louis Vuitton Dolomites Classic Run.

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1014 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that in vintage rally driving, there are generally two types of competitor.
  • Gianandrea Redaelli, a car nut whose family has long roots in the Italian printing business, is firmly in the “road book” camp.
  • Venice might not seem the most logical starting line for a car rally given the proverbial wetness of the streets.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that in vintage rally driving, there are generally two types of competitor. Both share a passion for keeping priceless and nearly century-old vehicles in use on the open road rather than displaying them under glass. But some see the drive itself as challenge enough, while stalwarts adhere to what’s called the road book. This is a hundred or so pages of complex navigational directions that the copilot uses to navigate instead of a map, maintaining a constant flow of instructions to the driver. It is this book and how closely you follow it that decides the eventual winner.

Gianandrea Redaelli, a car nut whose family has long roots in the Italian printing business, is firmly in the “road book” camp. In early September, I climbed into the copilot seat of his 1939 Aston Martin C-Type Speed Model Roadster Bertelli—just one of two ever built, with an experimental aerodynamic body that earned it the nickname “the Flying Pea”—and stayed there as he drove six hundred kilometers of “left at the traffic lights, right at the cow” for the Louis Vuitton Dolomites Classic Run. The rally started in Venice and ended, after a scenic but challenging detour high into the Dolomite mountains, at Monza, the home of Italian Formula 1, just in time for practice day of the Grand Prix.

Venice might not seem the most logical starting line for a car rally given the proverbial wetness of the streets. But the city was chosen this year because it was also the end point of the last LV rally of its kind: the La Serenissima Run from Monte Carlo to Venice in 2012. Gianandrea won that one as copilot, with his father, Giuseppe, at the wheel. The pair also won the one before it—the Boheme across Hungary, the Czech Republic, and Austria—in 2006. This time, however, the pressure was on me too.

I have been a copilot before, and I can tell you it’s no picnic. Rally racing in vintage cars is less about speed and more about timing. It’s an exercise that requires pinpoint accuracy at the time-stamp points in the overall course and, most critically, in the regularities. These are fiendishly short time-over-distance sections in which crossing the line just a few hundredths of a second late—or early—earns strict penalties. Sensibly, the day before the race began, Gianandrea took me out in the Aston in the Veneto countryside to practice, especially those critical regularities.

I could have opted for an easy life. The rally allowed competing cars, dating from 1931 to 1969, to use the road book or follow the course using a map in a dedicated phone app. But where’s the fun in that?

Industry observers note that “If you join a competition, you follow the regulations and strive to do your best,” Gianandrea claims. “As an Italian, if you paint numbers on the door of my car, I will want to win.”.

Recent findings suggest that every car in a rally like this comes with its own idiosyncrasies. On flat ground, someone driving a souped-up 2026 sports car would find these tests difficult to nail. In the reality of race conditions, the regularities often involve steep climbs or descents and unexpected corners, alling for an expert hand at the wheel—and foot on the gas pedal. The tendency of some car doors to swing open at hard bends (ours has the “suicide” doors with hinges on the back instead of the front, beloved by early carmakers) only adds to the excitement. The purpose of driver and copilot is to battle and overcome all the mechanical and computational challenges—and get our ride to the finish line bang on time.

Louis Vuitton has been involved in these glamorous and exacting vintage rallies since 1993. The Dolomites Run represents an enthusiastic return to the genre after a fourteen-year gap and, perhaps tellingly, the company’s global sponsorship (since 2025) of Formula 1. Unconfirmed rumors circulated in the field that the choice of ending the rally at a Grand Prix could well be repeated—and soon—in other countries in the future.

It has been revealed that it’s easy, after all, to see why a fusion of style and cars with six- and seven-figure price tags might appeal to Louis Vuitton and competitors alike. Not surprisingly, at every coffee and lunch stop, the LV effect sprinkled the race with an added sense of luxury. In between, our snaking caravan carried the glamour of a century of motoring along with it. At every hairpin you got a glimpse of a gull-wing Mercedes, a 1931 Bugatti two-seater (my personal fave), and a shimmering behemoth of a Bentley in quick succession. These cars would turn heads anywhere. But in Italy, arguably the home of the sports car, they brought smiles, applause, and gasps in even the tiniest village that passed by in our slipstream. I swear I even saw a nun with a glint in her eye at one set of traffic lights.

Navigating, I was rapidly learning, is not so much about providing a constant babble of information as it is knowing how to give clear and simple instructions—and only when strictly needed. As the finish neared in Monza at the end of two long days on the road, I was able to give Gianandrea the most helpful instruction of all: “Nothing for 15 kilometers.”.

“That,” he very kindly replied, “is the mark of a pro.”.

It has been revealed that even after the engines cooled, we were still clueless about how well we’d done overall. That changed at the final event, a dinner inside the Sforzesco Castle in Milan. Gianandrea stepped up, beaming, as winner of the race, and for the first time as driver. I stood somewhat sheepishly behind him as copilot as he received the trophy from Pietro Beccari, CEO of both Louis Vuitton and Louis Vuitton Fashion Group. It was an impressive swirl of Murano glass created by Venini, housed in its own equally impressive traveling case, made (naturellement) at Louis Vuitton’s atelier in Asnières.

Gianandrea has promised me visiting rights.

Morando ultimately revealed how he proposed to Cyrus. There were talks before we went about me popping the question but I was trying to keep it secret. She was not trying to keep it a secret, if you know what I mean. So I had to be really sneaky about it. We went to Tokyo first for a couple days and then on to Kyoto. I think she had a sense that it was coming, so I was waiting until the very last moment of the very last day to throw her off the scent as much as I could.”.

“We took a walk around the hotel grounds,” he continued. “There was this little outer garden that you had to cross a plank to get over. There was a sign that said you couldn’t cross; I was like, ‘That’s crazy, let’s go over there.’ She’s like, ‘No, it’s blocked.’ Eventually I persuaded her and we walked in and it was a little dead end, this beautiful Japanese forest-y situation. She was taking videos, and was turned away. That’s when I got on one knee and tapped her on the shoulder.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You’ve manifested several milestones—job, apartment, a squad of ride-or-dies. Now, you need a way to get from one to the other. This is where State Farm comes in as your trusted partner to help you make informed decisions. Here’s what you’ll need to know before you enter your car owner era.

As images of weekend getaways and road trips with your besties fill your mind, so, too, should these pre-purchase considerations.

At the dealership, put on your negotiation face. Buying a car is a little like dating—you do need to be observant, but you shouldn’t put all your cards (in this case: your budget) on the table. Finally, don’t be afraid to walk away. Follow these tips to make sure you're setting yourself up for success.

Before you turn up your favorite song and hit the open road, make sure your new baby is protected. It can be a lot to take in, so let’s demystify insurance. Here’s what you need to know.

Sources indicate that rate: This is the baseline estimated price that would cover the potential cost of future claims. It’s determined using shared group factors such as age group; if you’re in your twenties, it would take into account the statistical driving information for other 25-year-olds in a region.

Recent findings suggest that premium: This is the adjusted individual insurance price that you’ll pay over a six- or 12-month period. It’s created by starting with the rate, then adding more specific factors that affect your claim risk level. These include your driving record, claims history, mileage usage, and vehicle type.

Recent findings suggest that overwhelmed? Don’t sweat it—State Farm can get you an insurance quote before you buy.

Ah, the eternal question. Are you commitment-minded or more of a free agent?

To answer that when it comes to car ownership, consider how much you drive annually (to avoid leasing mileage overages if you exceed the stated mileage), how long you initiative to keep your vehicle, and your financial situation.

Then, know that there are insurance differences between leasing and buying, too. Leasing companies adhere to stricter requirements than those that most states set, which could translate into higher monthly premiums.

Industry observers note that if you buy to avoid the mileage caps and wear-and-tear of leasing, but still want the benefits of a fresh ride every few years, there is a moment during your payment strategy when you can get a new car. Your initial loan payments largely go to interest (what lenders charge for giving you money), but there’s a break-even point when your payments begin going to principal (the actual amount you’ve borrowed). When that happens, and the outstanding balance is equal to the value of the car, you can trade it in for that amount, which is a budget-friendly way to upgrade.

Whatever you choose, a little strategy will keep you in the driver’s seat from dreaming about your new car to signing on the dotted line.

State Farm is there to protect you and your car.

“It’s just amazing to see her keep going to the table,” he said of her music career. “Keep finding upcoming things to write about. Keep finding new melodies and things like that. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Miley Cyrus’s family has had so much drama going on over the last four years, I can only assume producers over at E! are presently trying to sign them up for a reality show. And tbh, we’d tune in. But if you haven’t been Keeping Up With the Cyruses, gather round because it’s equal parts complicated and messy.

Recent findings suggest that the short version: Everyone picked sides when Tish Cyrus and Billy Ray Cyrus got divorced, but after years of feuding, it seems the family may have buried the hatchet to all come together for Miley’s wedding...for now, anyway. Baffled? Same, so let’s dive in.

Tish filed for divorce from Billy Ray in April 2022, and they released the following joint statement to People:.

According to recent reports, I mean, sounds pretty chill! But Tish has since claimed she put up with “disrespect in every form” during the marriage, so...it seems like there was more going on behind the scenes than fans initially thought.

In fact, just a few months after Tish and Billy’s split announcement, a source told E! News that “the divorce between her parents has put a strain on [Miley’s] relationship with her dad and it’s been hard to connect with him in the last year. She hopes they can eventually work on their relationship.”.

Tish married Prison Break star Dominic Purcell in August 2023, and the internet was quick to clock that neither Noah Cyrus nor Braison Cyrus were in the bridal party (whereas Miley Cyrus, Brandi Cyrus, and Trace Cyrus were).

Instead, Noah and Braison seemingly spent the day chilling at Walmart and posted a selfie that featured Noah in a Billy Ray Cyrus t-shirt.

A few months after, a source confirmed to Us Weekly that Noah has “always been close with Billy Ray,” adding that this has also “caused a rift between her and Miley.”.

Oh, and another insider claimed, “The family dynamics haven’t been the same since the divorce, and now that Tish and Billy Ray are with other people, there’s even more division among them all.”.

While Miley and her sister have historically been close, fans spotted the first signs of drama in October 2023, when Noah wrote, “The disrespect in this video...” in the comment section of a clip of Miley on The Joe Rogan Experience.

Right around the same time, Billy Ray married Firerose—but it’s unclear whether any of Billy’s children were in attendance.

After winning an award at the 2024 Grammys, Miley left Billy out of her acceptance speech, and a source later told Us Weekly that he’d been attempting to reach out with congratulations.

“He’s tried reaching out to Miley many times and congratulated her on her Grammys,” the insider mentioned. “The kids have chosen sides, but friends are hoping the rift doesn’t last forever. Miley and Billy Ray are on the outs. Miley’s very close with her mom and is standing by her.”.

Another source put it more simply, saying, “Miley hasn’t gotten over the disrespect she feels Billy Ray demonstrated Tish and the family.”.

Later on in the month, in a truly wild plot twist, an insider alleged to Us Weekly, “Noah was [seeing] Dominic when Tish started pursuing him,” adding Tish “was aware" of the situation and that “the turmoil between Noah and Tish goes far beyond [what people think]. Noah is very distraught over Tish stealing Dominic from her.”.

Crucial note: Tish later claimed that she and Dominic met via DMs and did not mention anything about Noah...

Us Weekly also spoke to a source who remarked, “Noah and Tish haven’t spoken since the whole thing happened with Dominic,” and that “Tish is spiraling out of control and trying to figure out how to defuse this.” According to this person, Noah and Dominic were dating for “about eight to nine months” but were “having concerns.”.

According to recent reports, however! The Daily Mail spoke to an anonymous insider who claimed, “Noah never dated Dominic and they were not together. She is delusional to think otherwise and is trying to create a narrative that will paint her as a victim.” This source emphasized that “Noah was not invited to Tish’s wedding and she would not have come even if she was. Tish wanted a peaceful wedding and did not want Noah to create any sort of scene.”.

The insider went on to add, “Noah has always craved the attention because she did not get it growing up. Tish was always so Miley-sided because that is where the money was. Miley and Tish are like sisters and Noah has always been envious of this because she’s never had a connection with Tish like Miley has.”.

Recent findings suggest that when it comes to whether or not Miley knew about Noah and Dominic, sources differ. One person told People, “Miley had no idea about the drama with Dominic” and “confronted her mom about it,” while another told Us Weekly that Miley “absolutely knew” and was “fully aware.” Yikes!!!!

Yep! The musician shared a birthday message on Instagram for her mom in May amid the duo’s alleged feud alongside the caption, “Happy Birthday Mom.”.

Aaaaaaand by July, the two were seen out and about together in Los Angeles.

It has been revealed that during her My Next Guest Needs No Introduction episode, which aired in June, Miley explained (per E!), “Honestly, my mom is my hero. My father—I’m grateful for being able to watch him ahead of me. He’s almost given me this map. There is a map of what to do and what not to do. And he’s guided me on both.”.

According to recent reports, she continued, “My dad had a really rough childhood. And my childhood—I mean, we can go and talk about the hard times or the struggles—but I had food, I had love, I grew up in a beautiful big house and my dad didn’t have that.”.

Miley’s rare comments were aired amid Billy Ray filing for divorce from Firerose after seven months of marriage due to irreconcilable differences and “inappropriate marital conduct.”.

According to recent reports, following his dad’s performance at Trump’s inauguration Liberty Ball, Trace posted an open letter to Billy on Instagram, expressing concern for his health. Trace noted, “Me and the girls have been genuinely worried about you for years but you’ve pushed all of us away.”.

According to recent reports, he went on to add, “Noah desperately has wanted you to be a part of her life and you haven’t even been there for her. That’s your baby girl. She deserves better. Somehow just like me she still idolizes you though.”.

Apparently, Billy Ray later threatened him with “legal action” for his public plea, because three days later, Trace followed up with since-deleted IG note, explaining that his open letter “was beyond loving” and that he “could have been extremely honest about a lot more.”.

Billy ended up making a cryptic statement, saying, “Giving thanks for the California Rain . Praying for the brokenhearted and their pain. Praying for my family. For my children … sons and daughters…and their mother. Let this moment be the start of healing ❤️‍🩹 for us all. ‘The past does not equal the future.’ Amen.”.

After Trace’s open letter to Billy Ray went viral, Braison (who helped Billy produce his latest album) took to his IG Stories to respond to his older bro, noting that their dad was “happy, healthy, and ready to make this record.”.

A fan then slid into Trace’s DMs to question Braison’s post, and Trace replied with this cryptic message: “Birds of a feather flock together.” Well then!

In a recent development, meanwhile, a “Cyrus family source” told People that family was attempting to work things out. “They got through the drama of 2024, and it’s a new year,” the source remarked. “Miley and Noah and Braison and Tish, they don’t want to be this Cyrus family feud. This is not enjoyable for them.”.

Per a source for People, “Miley used to feel overwhelmed by the family drama. She worked hard to remove herself. She’s not about to get involved again. She’s in a great place now. She’s thriving and looking out for herself.”.

For Braison’s 31st birthday, Miley and her fiancé Maxx Morando joined Billy on his farm in Tennessee, and her dad snapped a cute selfie to prove it.

According to recent reports, during a profile with The Newly introduced York Times that same month, Miley revealed that she and Billy have healed their bond. “As I’ve gotten older, I’m respecting my parents as individuals instead of as parents—because my mom really loved my dad for her whole life, and I think being married to someone in the music industry and not being a part of it is obviously really hard,” Miley said at the time. “And so I think I took on some of my mom’s hurt as my own because it hurt her more than it hurt me as an adult, and so I owned a lot of her pain.”.

She added, “But now that my mom is so in love with my stepdad, who I completely adore, and now that my dad, I see him finding happiness, too—I can love them both as individuals instead of as a parental pairing.”.

The following month, during an interview on Monica Lewinsky’s podcast, Miley opened up about “Secrets” off the deluxe edition of her album Something Beautiful.

Industry observers note that “I wrote this song about my dad, because I wanted him to tell me even though there were secrets, even though I didn't really want to know,” she explained. “I wanted to be the one he felt safe enough to tell me the things that were damning and damaging to the family. I wanted him to think that as a middle child, I’m old enough that I could take some of that.”.

Sources indicate that she also talked about where her family stood in general, saying, “My family and I have had a really difficult…What did you call your decade? Dark decade. Yeah, we had one of those.”.

She continued, “Half of us weren't speaking to each other at one point, and we cleaned all that up. That was a really important part of my year this year, was all of my family putting those lines of communication back together. A lot because of, you know, I had a lot of loyalty to my mom, the way that families do when parents get divorced.”.

Miley sat down with her mom and sisters for an interview with The Cut, where it was revealed that the Cyrus ladies are all on good terms.

At one point, Miley remarked, “One thing I’ve always loved about our family is that we’re very honorable and respectful of each other’s differences; I think a lot of families get torn apart from their differences...but as we’ve gotten older, we’ve found our own opinions and ideas individually.”.

To celebrate 20 years of Hannah Montana, Miley starred in a TV special, during which both of her parents made appearances.

Miley tied the knot with Maxx in Palm Springs, where—according to a source for People—“the most special part was seeing Miley’s family all come together to celebrate her.”.

In attendance were Miley’s parents Tish and Billy, Billy’s girlfriend Elizabeth Hurley and her son Damian Hurley, Tish’s husband Dominic, Miley’s sister Noah and her fiancé Pinkus, and Miley’s sister Brandi and her fiancé Matt Southcombe.

It’s unclear, however, whether Miley’s brothers Trace and Braison (or her half-brother Christopher Cody) were there.
