📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that our goal was 50—just 50!—of the best-dressed people of the year, a list to commemorate the unforgettable fashion moments of a very topsy-turvy 2026. Sounds easy…but, well, list-making never is. There were athletes who turned game days into runways, actors who owned the red carpet and the sidewalk, and method-dressing movie stars who artfully ignored the meaning of the word cut.

Sources indicate that we wanted them all, plus some highly fashionable characters from unexpected fields and walks of life, and we wanted couples, which we insisted should be counted as singletons (a technicality!). We struggled and horse-traded and voted and arrived finally at…55! (The same number as last year.) Here is the fruit of our labor: an unranked, diligently categorized, highly subjective list of Vogue’s best dressed of 2026. And it all begins with our cover star, a selection that was the result of a rather heated debate. Enjoy!

Written by: Christian Allaire, Margaux Anbouba, Taylor Antrim, Max Berlinger, Laird Borrelli-Persson, Anna Cafolla, Liam Hess, Alexandra Hildreth, Hannah Jackson, Joan Kennedy, Irene Kim, Anna Grace Lee, Nicole Phelps, Madeleine Schulz, and Emma Specter.

Vogue’s Best Dressed cover star is….

Sources indicate that STORRIE TIME Conner Storrie brings the Ken-ergy in a miniaturized version of his Gucci Best Dressed cover look. Coach watch pendant.

Why 2026 was his year: Playing brooding Russian hockey player Ilya Rozanov in the gay romance Heated Rivalry—in various states of deshabille—released this 26-year-old Hollywood hopeful waiting tables in Los Angeles to cultural supernova. His last 12 months have seen a kind of fashion miracle: Storrie is now better known for what he wears than what he doesn’t. Click here for his cover-story conversation with Chloe Malle—which ranged from Storrie’s punk roots to his adoration of Parker Posey, his side hustle in “provocateur” photography, and more.

Friends, lovers, collaborators—occasionally all at once.

Spector and Hall wear Tom Ford.

Why 2026 was their year: Him: Train Daddy in The Gilded Age; Her: Wicked stepmother in Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story (and more).

Their couple style, in essence: Hudson Valley cabincore meets Tom Ford heat.

Kravitz wears The Row. Styles wears The Row and Adidas.

Their year in fashion: Excellent outerwear, statement headgear, rave-ready sunglasses, plenty of The Row.

Their couple style, in essence: Kiss all the time. Dress alike, more than occasionally.

From left: Imhof wears Balenciaga, Teuscher wears Rodarte; both wear Valentino.

Why 2026 was their year: Teuscher traded Lincoln Center for Hong Kong to star in her partner Imhof’s queer, Shakespearean House of Swans.

Their couple style, in essence: Berghain Romeo and Juliet.

Barone in Missoni; Skinner in ERL.

Why 2026 was their year: Barone released comedy special Galaxy Brain; Skinner got to work on Overcompensating season 2. Together: their riotous podcast, Ride, and Halloween domination.

Their couple style, in essence: Newport Beach heartthrobs, if they canvassed for Zohran.

Left: Both in Dior. Right: Arquette wears Circus of Magdela; Lean wears Giorgio Armani.

Why 2026 was their year: Lean bringing down the house at the VMAs, while writing duets with Arquette; the couple hard-launching at Dior Men’s spring 2027 show.

Their couple style, in essence: Shades of blue (or bleu).

Left: Rosalía in Stella McCartney. Right: Bahia wears Saint Laurent; Rosalía wears Vivienne Westwood.

Their year in fashion: Contrasting-yet-coordinated masc-for-femme dressing, conjuring early days Justin and Hailey.

Why we can’t get enough: Two words: tooth necklace.

Johnson wears a Nour Hammour coat.

He mentioned; she said: MGK to Vogue: “I started kind of respecting my upkeep, and I’ve watched things open up.” Johnson to Vogue: “[Musicians] like me, I don’t know what to say.”.

Industry observers note that their couple style, in essence: Hoodies, diamonds, beanies, grommets, lace, leather, fangs. Misery business.

Industry observers note that LIFE IN PLASTIC, IT’S FANTASTIC! Master of the step-and-repeat, Kendall Jenner set the gold standard for polka-dots in her Valentino Academy Gala dress.

The category is: great gowns, beautiful gowns.

Jenner wears Armani; Alexander Calder earrings.

Her year in fashion: Winged Victory at the Met, snagging ultra-rare Calder earrings for her first Lido, spreading the gospel of The Row, and perfecting polka dots at the Academy Gala.

Why we can’t get enough: She wears clothes like it’s her job.

Why 2026 was her year: Rose, Fatherland, and Project Hail Mary! (And, ahem, Digger.).

Highlight reel: Matières Fécales’ riff on the bar suit; Chanel’s riff on the hedgehog.

Her year in fashion: Dior standouts (acid green Poiret punk and impressionistic water lilies, specifically), plus an Issey Miyake breastplate, Marc Jacobs sequins, and Lii color blocking.

Best look of 2026: That star-spangled scarlet High Sport halter dress with a swishy fringed hem for the London premiere of Toy Story 5—a clever, playful wink to the film’s universe that still felt fashion.

Mulligan wears (from left): Colleen Allen; Dries Van Noten; The Row; Celine.

Why 2026 was her year: Lending her voice to Wildwood, scoring an Emmy nom for Beef season 2, getting a CBE from the King (she wore The Row).

Best look: That triptych of pixelated floral brocades from Julian Klausner’s fall 2026 Dries Van Noten collection. Bonus points for the pockets in the top!

Why this was her year: An awards-season run for Hamnet; an ultra-chic stint on the jury at Cannes.

Best look of 2026: Schiaparelli’s spiky “Isabella Blowfish” dress was a creepy-cheeky wow on the runway—and doubly satisfying on the Croisette.

A DOLL’S HOUSE Who indicates you can only wear your Met Gala dress once? Back in her Barbie Dreamhouse closet, Paloma Elsesser plays dress-up in her bespoke Bureau of Imagination gown.

They’re wearing your favorite brand—you just don’t know it yet.

Elsesser wears (from left): Junya Watanabe; Comme des Garçons, Phoebe Philo shoes, Chanel bag; Goyagoma.

Why 2026 was her year: When she wasn’t on the hunt for her next vintage deep cut? Hitting the runway for Ferragamo and Junya Watanabe and debuting Francesco Risso’s Bureau of Imagination at the Met.

She’ll get bragging rights for: The Bureau of Imagination gown—patchworked, painted, and embellished by “a squadron of people.” A true one-of-a-kind.

Thompson wears Giovanna Flores; Kallmeyer.

Why 2026 was her year: A Golden Globes nomination for Hedda; the runaway thriller His & Hers; and her Broadway debut in Fear of 13 alongside Adrien Brody.

She’ll get bragging rights for: Her support of all things indie is as evident in her work as in her wardrobe: just take the enviably cool Giovanna Flores patchwork dress she wore on a sweltering day in New York.

Peak wears (from left): Lii; Diotima; Torishéju.

Why 2026 was her year: She drummed up Hunger Games hype, toggling her looks between indie darlings and bona fide fashion-girl pulls.

She’ll get bragging rights for wearing: A scrunched-up black top and red cut-out leather skirt from London-based Torishéju; the standout textured Diotima dress from this season; and Fresh York favorite Liii.

Ortega wears Pierre Cardin; Elias Matso.

She’ll get bragging rights for wearing: A custom dress from Polimoda fashion school graduate Elias Matso, made entirely from steel boning and beads in a process that took over 300 hours.

Her year in fashion: Ditching goth—at least until Wednesday season 3.

OUT OF THE BOX On the lively streets of Fresh York City, Sarah Pidgeon does her best CBK in a leopard-print Adam Lippes coat. Susan Alexandra pigeon charm.

Pigeon wears Chanel; Yohji Yamamoto.

Why 2026 was her year: She introduced a fresh generation to Carolyn Bessette-Kennedy—and her Yohji Yamamoto-filled closet—in Love Story.

Give her an Oscar for this look: The lacy aqua blue slip dress she wore to the Chanel Pre-Oscars party married CBK-ish ’90s minimalism with present-day Blazy-mania.

Zendaya wears Matières Fécales.

Why 2026 was her year: The Drama! Spider-Man! The Odyssey! Dune! Oh, and she found time to marry Tom Holland, too.

Give her an Oscar for this look: The white strapless Matières Fécales gown with matching feathered wings while promoting The Odyssey was pure Athena realness.

Edgar-Jones wears (from left): Miu Miu; Andreas Kronthaler for Vivienne Westwood; Rodarte.

Why 2026 was her year: The 18th-century-inspired Sense and Sensibility press tour, featuring a dreamy blush Galliano jacket worn with jeans; sexed-up pantaloon sets from Dries Van Noten and Colleen Allen; and lots and lots of Stella McCartney-era Chloé.

Up next: Going toe-to-toe with Michelle Williams in A Place in Hell and bringing another book club favorite to the big screen in Tomorrow, and Tomorrow, and Tomorrow.

Robbie wears Schiaparelli; Dilara Findikoglu.

Why we can’t get enough: Schiaparelli couture with Elizabeth Taylor’s legendary Taj Mahal diamonds one day, cutoff jorts the next.

Up Next: How will she method-dress for Untitled Ocean’s Eleven Prequel?

Fanning wears (from left): Robert Wun; Givenchy by Sarah Burton; Evan Clayton.

Why 2026 was her year: Earned her first Oscar nomination for Sentimental Value, delivered Margot’s Got Money Troubles, and dressed in her Capitol best for The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.

Her style, in essence: Anything can be a hat!

It has been revealed that OFF THE SHELF Olivia Rodrigo, here in vintage Rudi Gernreich, brought major flower power with her inaugural Daisy Chain Fields festival. Susan Alexandra flower and mushroom charms.

Pop stars or politicians—they’re all headliners to us.

Rodrigo wears Versace; Hussein Chalayan.

Why 2026 was her year: It was a legacy-defining one between Rodrigo’s best album yet (hello, seven Grammy nominations) and her inaugural Daisy Chain Fields music festival, which raised $20 million to support nonprofits for women and girls.

Her year in fashion: She joined a long line of badasses who’ve subverted the babydoll dress—Kathleen Hanna and Courtney Love come to mind.

Michelle Obama wears Acne Studios.

Why we can’t get enough: From this summer’s ribbon-cutting at the Barack Obama Presidential Center in Thom Browne to attending the U.S. Open in red, white, and blue Chanel, she makes patriotism look chic.

The look that deserved a push notification: The Acne Studios skirt custom-printed with a photo of her late mother Marian Robinson, a gesture that brought the former president—and the rest of us—to tears.

Dion wears (from left): Tom Ford; Dior; Chanel; Chanel.

Why 2026 was their year: A triumphant return to the stage following her stiff person syndrome diagnosis meant 16 sold-out demonstrates at Paris’s Plénitude Arena, plus daily pap walks outside of Le Royal Monceau.

The look that deserved a push notification: The custom Chanel sweetheart-neckline gown that took 1,380 hours to make—a recreation of her 1997 Oscars dress. Our hearts will go on!

Why 2026 was her year: Wrestling with mortality on Lost Weekend; stealing scenes in Primetime.

The look that deserved a push notification: In Venice, a lesson in indie-darling dressing: Gucci skirt suit, below-the-knee tattoo, visible leg hair.

Flanagan wears Sky-Eagle Collection.

Why 2026 was her year: The Minnesota senator-to-be’s midterm victory made her the first-ever Indigenous woman elected to the United States Senate.

The look that deserved a push notification: Victory called for a sleek burgundy suit and a traditional pair of dentalium shell earrings by Yurok artist Jessica Mendez.

TINY FURNITURE Just like Mary, Cole Escola is the picture-perfect homemaker in the Christopher John Rogers jumpsuit they wore to the Tonys. Movado watch. Jennifer Behr earrings.

Imitation may be the sincerest form of flattery, but there’s no replicating one-of-one style.

Escola wears (from left): Chanel; Eckhaus Latta; vintage Eve Stillman.

Why 2026 was their year: Oh, Mary! went on the road, and Escola’s Miss Piggy became the in-the-works screenplay we didn’t know we needed.

Highlight reel: Coco cosplay at Chanel couture; an “ibuprofen”-pink Christopher John Rogers jumpsuit at the Tonys; an Eckhaus Latta deep cut at the CFDA Awards.

Taylor wears Schiaparelli; Thom Browne.

Why 2026 was her year: Who else could collect their Golden Globe in a bejeweled Schiaparelli whale tail?

Sources indicate that her best look: The trompe l’oeil Thom Browne at the SAG Awards, with her daughter Rue Rose on hand to adjust her train. As Taylor put it: “A very expensive stylist.”.

Why 2026 was his year: A longtime Comme des Garçons acolyte, Sedaris promoted his latest book, The Land and Its People, in layers of deconstructed tailoring, voluminous skirts, and oddball shoes.

Why we can’t get enough: Dressed in a diaphanous layered ensemble for Late Night With Seth Meyers, he quipped, “I think of this as a sports skirt.”.

Ellis Ross wears (from left): Prada; Balenciaga; Dries Van Noten.

Why this was her year: A Broadway debut in Every Brilliant Thing, an expanding Pattern Beauty lineup, a daytime Emmy for her show, Solo Traveling—and she found time to start styling herself.

Best look of 2026: That marigold Balenciaga at the 2026 Academy Museum Gala; beautifully textured, quintessentially her (with a dash of Law Roach).

Industry observers note that why we can’t get enough: What was the American Hagwon author’s first fashion flex when fiction started paying the bills? Early days Thom Browne. “I bought one of Thom’s first sweaters,” Lee told Vogue.

Best look of 2026: Her go-to matching pinstriped Comme des Garçons blazer and dress for large speaking events. Who said a uniform can’t have style?

Hill wears (from left): Bottega Veneta; Saint Laurent; Balenciaga.

Why 2026 was her year: Became a BET Living Legend in voluminous, ruffled Saint Laurent with wrap-around sunglasses; reunited with Wyclef to celebrate the 30th anniversary of The Score; sat front row at Balenciaga spring 2027 as “Ready or Not” blared.

Her style in essence: Can’t take my eyes off you.

PAPER DOLL Audrey Nuna puts a bow on 2026 in the Thom Browne cape she wore to the Golden Globes.

You’ll never again have to ask, “Wait, where do I know them from?”.

Nuna wears Maison Margiela; Thom Browne.

Where you know her from: If you don’t know her face, odds are you’ve heard her sing: Nuna lent her voice to Mira in the Oscar- and Grammy-winning KPop Demon Hunters.

Best outfit of 2026: The cocoon-like black cape dress embellished with bows from Thom Browne—one of her more understated looks, if you can believe it.

You’ve heard them: Honking on their Getting Killed tour, SNL, or frontman Cameron Winter’s Carnegie Hall live album.

According to recent reports, their year in fashion: Well-worn band tees, threadbare tank tops, bug-eyed sunglasses, and dresses over jeans are par for the course. Their too-cool-for-school style is just that: too cool.

Lenae wears Natasha Zinko; Rabanne.

Why you should know her: The singer was marked safe from one-hit-wonderdom with her third album, Blue Island.

Best outfit of 2026: The eccentric, richly embellished Space Age Rabanne dress she wore to the Grammys was totally out of this world.

Where you know her from: Apple TV’s Shrinking and Kane Parsons’s instant horror classic Backrooms.

In a recent development, best outfit of 2026: The peachy fall 2011 Prada minidress with rounded sleeves, sharp front pleats, and a belted drop waist that she wore during the Toronto International Film Festival. If Miuccia hasn’t already come calling…she should.

Sui Wonders wears Miss Sohee; Anna Sui.

Why you should know her: The actor—and niece of fashion designer Anna Sui—proved good taste is genetic while making the rounds for I Want Your Sex and The Studio.

Best outfit of 2026: At Sundance, she plumbed the family archives, settling on a funky, faux fur-trimmed slip dress and matching bonnet. She got it from her auntie!

Great on the red carpet; even better on a morning-after coffee run.

Lawrence wears (from left): Dior jacket, Completedworks earrings; The Row polo, Siedrés pants, Tory Burch necklace, The Row loafers; Junk Food T-shirt, Dries Van Noten skirt, Ancient Greek slippers, Hermès bag.

Her style, in essence: Skate park chaperone.

Jacobson wears (from left): Khaite; Dilara Findikoglu; Mel Usine; Conner Ives.

Why we can’t get enough: The theatricality we want from a Yale Drama grad: high collars, slashed abs, daring necklines, sleek layering.

Recent findings suggest that on the clock: Her 2026 Met Gala look—as a Joan of Arc-esque figure in a coin-and-pin-adorned armored bodysuit by Dilara Findikoglu. Biopic when?

Edebiri wears (from left): Conner Ives; Giovanna Flores; vintage tee, Still Kelly pants, Chanel bag.

Why this was her year: Post-Bear, trying upcoming things with her career (Broadway; Woolf), and her fashion (Giovanna Flores patchwork dress; Chanel tail feathers).

Best look of 2026: She showed the boys how it’s done in a slick Conner Ives suit.

Schafer wears (from left): Prada; Gimaguas dress; Celine.

Best off-duty look of 2026: The silky purple backward button-up over a tomato-red Gimaguas minidress she wore down the Chateau Marmont driveway.

Her style, in essence: Up for anything, from Gustav Klimt’s Mäda Primavesi to dystopian fembot.

Abrams wears (from left): Balenciaga by Nicolas Ghesquière top, Hamish Olrik pants, Chanel shoes; Colleen Allen; vintage tee from Moth Food, Chanel pants, shoes, and bag.

Best off-duty look of 2026: The sporty, vintage-looking “Vote” baseball tee paired with high-waisted wool trousers and Chanel’s signature cap-toe shoes: effortless, elegant, utterly cool.

MVPs and benchwarmers alike stole the show with their ’fits this year.

Osaka wears Miss Claire Sullivan; Hana Yagi.

Her slam-dunk look: Acing Wimbledon whites in a Hana Yagi walkout look inspired by traditional Japanese ceremonial attire.

Clarkson wears (from left): Abercrombie & Fitch; vintage T-shirt, Louis Vuitton scarf, Hat Club hat; Chrome Hearts jacket, Saint Laurent pants.

Why 2026 was his year: Knicks in 5.

His slam-dunk look: A fitted black Rick Owens long-sleeve and pants amidst the Paris heatwave. He ditched the shirt post-show—not that we’re complaining.

Why 2026 was his year: A ruptured Achilles and dashed World Cup dreams didn’t keep the French footballer from Wimbledon or the Balenciaga front row.

His slam-dunk look: A Miu Miu Canadian tuxedo, vested for maximum bicep-baring.

They are not like other guys, in that you’ll never catch them in a snoozy black tux.

O’Connor wears (from left): Lemaire; vintage jacket, Adidas track pants; Hermès.

Best look of 2026: The all-black Hermès leather shirt-and-trousers ensemble that gagged the internet.

Sources indicate that why we can’t get enough: The swerve from tweedy London boy to louche fashion lad. We always knew he had it in him.

Why this was his year: Euphoria, Disclosure Day, and Michael (plus an Emmy nomination for The Four Seasons); shutting down every single step-and-repeat along the way.

Why 2026 was his year: From season 2 of Adults to the front rows of Paris Fashion Week, Innanen reminded us that he is far more than just a TikTok star.

Why we can’t get enough: On one New York City scorcher, he made it clear he was in heat in a Horny graphic tee.

Malkovich wears (from left): Dior; Chanel; Aubero.

Recent findings suggest that why 2026 was his year: Malkovich has always been a bona fide fashion obsessive (lest we forget his past ventures in menswear design as “Technobohemian”). Wild Horse Nine gave him the red carpets to prove it.

Breakout moment of 2026: The Dior suit with a ruff collar he wore at the Venice Film Festival was a cross between a Tudor courtier and frill-necked lizard.

They’re your favorite fashion editor’s favorite fashion editor…and stylist and buyer and model.

According to recent reports, on Marci: JW Anderson shirt, Ruadh jeans, Loewe bag. On Lori: Nahmias shirt, Chanel skirt, Alaïa bag.

Why the fashion industry loves them: No one inspires envy as consistently as aunt-niece duo Lori and Marci Hirshleifer, who operate the dynastic Manhasset store Hirshleifers.

Why 2026 was their year: At a time when everyone is looking to amp up their personal style, these two have it in spades.

Bellizzi wears (from left): Dior by John Galliano; Chanel; Versace.

Why 2026 was her year: After receiving an Oscar nomination for her work on Marty Supreme, Bellizzi styled her first Vogue shoot and pulled double duty at 6397’s spring 2027 show, both styling and walking in it.

Highlight reel: Galliano Dior, Blazy Chanel, Dario Versace.

Lebasi in Miss Claire Sullivan.

Why 2026 was her year: When she isn’t styling Vogue Italia shoots or walking the Conner Ives runway, Lebasi consults for CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund finalist Miss Claire Sullivan.

According to recent reports, best outfit: At the 2026 CFDA Fashion Fund Finalist cocktail, Lebasi elevated a white tee and blue jeans with a Miss Claire Sullivan bolero. Someone’s already got the 2027 Met Gala theme down.

Left: Rick Owens jacket, Afghani embroidered chapan, Sea trousers, Kero shoes, COS cummerbund, Chimi sunglasses. Right: Miu Miu pants and shoes, Prada button-up, Calvin Klein bra, Gentle Monster sunglasses.

Why this was her year: At the spring 2027 collections, the Swedish-Pakistani catwalker seemed to open (Fendi, Victoria Beckham, Sacai) or close (Tom Ford, Hermès, Louis Vuitton) every show that mattered.

Her best look: The teeny tank top and hip-slung jeans she was spotted wearing off-runway at Paris Fashion Week would get a nod of approval from Haider Ackermann, who put her in the season’s most barely-there bathing suit at Tom Ford.

Recent findings suggest that left: Ojuromi. Center: Ojuromi wears a dress by Debby Fasingha. Right: Fasingha.

In a recent development, why the fashion industry loves them: This duo grew their homespun, high-energy Lagos fashion showcases into a global sensation. Through Ojuromi and Fasingha’s lens, fashion feels fresh, personal, and full of possibility.

Why 2026 was their year: After a video of Ojuromi walking in Fasingha’s DIY, Chanel-inspired looks went viral, the model made her runway debut at the brand’s spring 2027 show.

Pumpkin Pie Bars

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, pumpkin pie bars are the easiest way to get the classic dessert on your Thanksgiving table.
  • Arrange a rack in center of oven and preheat it to 350°.
  • Industry observers note that press the dough evenly into prepared baking sheet, and bake until it is barely set and just starting to turn golden.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, pumpkin pie bars are the easiest way to get the classic dessert on your Thanksgiving table. They require no crust, chilling, or crimping. All you have to do is press the crust into the pan, pour on your filling, and you’re ready to go! Way less time, way more glory.

Arrange a rack in center of oven and preheat it to 350°. Grease a 12" x 17" baking sheet with cooking spray. In a large bowl, mix flour, butter, confectioners’ sugar, and salt until the mixture looks crumbly.

Industry observers note that press the dough evenly into prepared baking sheet, and bake until it is barely set and just starting to turn golden. This process should take about 20 minutes. In a large bowl, whisk pumpkin puree, cream, brown sugar, eggs, flour, cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, vanilla, and salt until smooth. Pour the filling over crust and bake until set and only slightly jiggly in the center. This should take about 40 minutes.

Let it cool completely before you cut the set mixture into squares.

In a recent development, dollop with whipped topping and dust with cinnamon before serving. Enjoy!

The full list of ingredients and instructions can be found in the recipe below.

According to recent reports, store leftover pumpkin pie bars in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 4 days. Add the whipped topping just before serving.

The Under-The-Radar Brands the Best Dressed List Loved in 2026

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1900 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vogue

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that vogue’s 2026 best dressed list certainly knows its way around a luxury label ambassadorship: Chanel swans, Saint Laurent savants, Dior devotees, Miu Miu girls and Prada protégés.
  • The distinction between under-the-radar and fashion-crowd famous is becoming increasingly blurred.
  • Greta Lee, Hunter Schafer, and Whitney Peak have embraced the retro-futurist designs of Zane Li’s Lii, the award-winning label crafted from his unassuming and tiny Chinatown studio.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that vogue’s 2026 best dressed list certainly knows its way around a luxury label ambassadorship: Chanel swans, Saint Laurent savants, Dior devotees, Miu Miu girls and Prada protégés. But along the way, you’ll find that some of this year’s most thrilling moments for ‘stepping out’ and ‘stunning’ (as per the celebrity style news cycle) came courtesy of designers whose names aren’t quite so familiar. For this particularly discerning crowd, an emerging designer and an IYKYK label carries just a bit more sartorial currency.

The distinction between under-the-radar and fashion-crowd famous is becoming increasingly blurred. Designers like Conner Ives and Rachel Scott’s Diotima have developed considerable celebrity followings and their fair share of viral moments, while labels like Kallmeyer are hardly insider secrets anymore. The next generation, however, is hot on their heels.

Greta Lee, Hunter Schafer, and Whitney Peak have embraced the retro-futurist designs of Zane Li’s Lii, the award-winning label crafted from his unassuming and tiny Chinatown studio. Tessa Thompson, Ayo Edebiri, and Paloma Elsesser, meanwhile, found plenty to love in Giovanna Flores’s free-form silhouettes, pattern agnosticism, and deadstock materials. Elsewhere, Elle Fanning indulged in the character play of August Barron, Jenna Ortega put a young designer’s extraordinary corsetry craftsmanship on the red carpet, and John Malkovich looked to upcycled lace. Rosalía has made something of a habit of championing emerging talent, with the likes of Yasmina Atta and Laura Andraschko finding a place in her expansive, prima ballerina meets bad-girl Mary Magdalene wardrobe.

More than a passing fascination with the next substantial thing, this year’s best dressed list has fostered relationships with designers in ways that speak to their genuine curiosity and enthusiasm about clothes, the people making them, and the exciting places fashion is heading. Below, the under-the-radar brands this year’s best dressed loved.

Greta lee wears Giovanna Flores.

In a recent development, brooklyn-based Giovanna Flores is a fast favorite among Hollywood’s most adventurous dressers for her scavenger-chic designs. Her work is often made using deadstock and recycled textiles, and utilizes unexpected fabric combinations, patchworking, and inventive draping. Paloma Elsesser dropped her polka dot bodice and zebra-hemmed G.F. fit amid one fab Instagram dump, and Tessa Thompson mixed her prints with a sumptuous Bordeaux sash. Ayo Edebiri opted for a mismatched strawberry seed and gingham number, while Greta Lee wore some canary yellow velvet. (Both Edebiri and Lee are styled by Danielle Goldberg and hold Chanel and Dior ambassador titles respectively—Flores’s spliced-and-diced one-of-ones are a must-have.).

Zane Li’s Lii is a fashion-crowd secret hiding in plain sight; this year, he netted the LVMH Karl Lagerfeld Prize for Innovation and was a CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund winner. Known for its architectural minimalism and precise construction in enchanting color combos, the Fresh York label has struck a major chord. Greta Lee, again, was an early champion, most recently wearing an architectural two-toned blue dress with a sexy thigh-high slit. Whitney Peak wore a twisted tank and skirt look fresh from the spring 2027 runway—a collection that unspooled the emotional threads between girlhood and womanhood, reflected in dramatically skewed tops and miniskirts in scuba materials and wide-eyed shades of teal and tomato. Hunter Schafer has incorporated the retro-futurist designs into her ongoing Blade Runner 2099 press tour. Consider Lii a modern fixture in the wardrobes of Hollywood’s experimental minimalists.

Another Yasmina Atta custom design.

Rosalía has spent the last year either en pointe or expounding the possibilities of a popstar’s wardrobe, oscillating between the ecclesiastical and the balletic. London-based, Nigerian-born designer Yasmina Atta, a Central Saint Martins graduate whose surrealist designs draw on African cinema, folklore, and subculture, was central to one of Rosalía’s most viral fashion moments. This was when she stepped out in Latest York in a custom Atta creation: a plunging, sheer bronze latex bodice, visible black lace lingerie, a dramatically dropped waist, and a frothy cream tutu, all cinched with studded belts—a look partly inspired by Edgar Degas’s Little Dancer Aged Fourteen. (Rosalía had also worn a slate-gray wool minidress by the designer earlier in the year.) For a musician whose Lux era has been defined by religious iconography and the discipline of dance, Atta’s fantastical yet fervent approach to fashion is a perfect fit.

Rosalia wears Laura Andraschko.

Laura Andraschko’s hedonistic, subculture-informed designs also found a fan in Rosalía. The Berlin- and Vienna-raised Central Saint Martins graduate draws on various influences: indie sleaze and nightlife, aristocrats, Sloane Rangers, and Alpine bunny glam. Rosalía has worn the designer on several occasions: at the 2026 US Open, she chose an Andraschko T-shirt, while a previous Paris outing saw her in a khaki minidress from the fall 2025 Après Ski collection, with a dramatic furry hem and velvet-trimmed, off-the-shoulder neckline. More recently, of course, she had to pull on a tutu-like skirt. It’s feminine and anarchic and exactly right for Rosalía.

Jenna Ortega wears Elias Matso.

Jenna Ortega and her stylist Enrique Melendez spent last year crafting a deviant glam-goth wardrobe for the Wednesday star. This year, we’ve witnessed a subtle evolution into freer experiments with color and textiles. For a Newly introduced York screening of Klara and the Sun, Ortega wore a sculptural creation by young designer Elias Matso, made from steel corset boning and 6,500 beads, all inspired by the colors of painter Marc Ranger. The Polimoda graduate’s approach to corsetry is theatrical and technically audacious, with references ranging from Bob Mackie to Charles James. The custom dress reportedly took more than 300 hours to make, and marked a major red carpet moment for a designer early in his career.

“This dress was a massive test of my free will and just how much I was willing to put towards something that did not have a guaranteed return,” Matso said. “It was scary, I felt crazy at times, I lost a lot of money, and now this object exists. After many blisters, rebuilds, failed trials, international shipping nightmares, and working on it in six different cities with so many helping hands it just exists, and that is wild.” A hand-crafting corsetier to know.

Elle Fanning wears August Barron.

According to recent reports, elle Fanning is all about the Effie-coded whimsy right now, and Paris-based August Barron has proven a kindred spirit in this quest. Formerly known as All-In, the label is the brainchild of Benjamin Barron and Bror August Vestbø, whose designs play with heady ideas of domesticity, nostalgia, and the conventions of femininity. Fanning made a memorable appearance in a pale yellow striped polo shirt and a voluminous, bow-adorned tulle skirt from their fall 2026 Bedtime Story collection. The design duo has a talent for taking familiar clothes and articulating something thrilling throught them. Whether referencing American pageant girls, cabaret queens, housewives, gay icons Judy or a Marilyn, August Barron provides the much-needed glitch in the glamour for those brave enough to dial in.

London-based GOYAGOMA was the talk of London Fashion Week when the label made its debut earlier this year at designer incubator Fashion East (the same one that birthed Simone Rocha, Martine Rose, and Grace Wales Bonner.) Of course, Paloma Elsesser picked up his designs fast, and previous best dressed honoree A$AP Rocky is a fan. Founded by Bahamian designer Traiceline Pratt, a Central Saint Martins graduate who previously worked with Phoebe Philo and A-Cold-Wall, the label draws on memories of growing up in the Bahamas to reimagine everyday clothing through luxe fabrications, exaggerated proportions, and determined tailoring. Elsesser’s endorsement adds to an already growing list of admirers of the designer’s assuredly off-beat approach to the capsule wardrobe—expect to see it hit Dover Street Market soon, too.

Julie Kegels takes her bow during spring 2027.

Antwerp-born Julie Kegels has established herself as one of the most interrogative young voices in European fashion, and both Paloma Elsesser and Rosalia have taken notice. A graduate of Antwerp’s Royal Academy of Fine Arts who went on to work at Alaïa, Kegels introduced her namesake label in 2024, exploring the tension between conventional feminine dressing and something more surreal. Her collections manipulate familiar silhouettes through draping and distortion, taking as much inspiration from working girls as she does from furniture. Winning the 2026 LVMH Prize has only accelerated her ascent—her signature thong socks are an even speedier way into the brand, or you could hold out for her aims to invest her LVMH prize money into the development of more shoes and bags.

Miyako Bellizzi styled and walked the spring 2027 show.

Sarah Pidgeon during a 6397 fitting.

Founded by Stella Ishii in 2013, with Lizzie Owens now leading design, New York label 6397 has built a quietly influential universe of lived-in separates and pieces that slyly riff on what “staples” can mean. Among its fans are Paloma Elsesser, Greta Lee, and Sarah Pidgeon. The brand’s debut runway show was styled by costume designer and best dressed lister Miyako Bellizzi, who also walked in the presentation. The downtown creative community has long embraced 6397, and this is the New York woman energy you just want to bottle.

Whitney Peak wears spring 2026, styled by Karla Welch.

According to recent reports, london-based Torishéju takes an experimental and emotive approach to pattern-cutting and construction: trained as a menswear designer, Torishéju Dumi has built a sartorial world that plays with trompe l’oeil and other-century costuming made modern, combining subversive design twists and classic craft techniques. Whitney Peak, on The Hunger Games press tour, opted for a deconstructed scarlet red leather skirt brought together by sensual draping and thigh-high cutouts, paired with a sculpted black halter top. This is the one for those who like their fashion with a little friction.

Ayo Edebiri wears Still Kelly pants.

According to recent reports, never underestimate the power of a great pair of trousers. And as Ayo Edebiri knows, the best off-duty outfits often hinge on an immaculate basic. Her choice? Still Kelly’s tailored black trousers worn with a vintage Björk T-shirt sourced by stylist Danielle Goldberg. The brand describes itself as a sartorial “slow burn.” “Building a world, making good products, it takes time,” founder Marc Kalman previously told Vogue. “I’m cool with that.”.

Louisa Jacobson wears Catalogue NYC.

Industry observers note that louisa Jacobson has never been one for fashion’s binaries. With stylist Edward Bowleg III, she delights in the push-and-pull of buttoned-up tailoring and daring exposure, masculine codes and feminine flourishes. Catalogue NYC is exactly the sort of emerging designer label that articulates that. Founded by former Peter Do designers Pablo Correa and An Nguyen alongside Vincent Ho, the New York brand approaches familiar wardrobe pieces with an experimental eye, proposing new ways of wearing tailoring and dresses. On Jacobson, those ideas find an exquisite home.

Sources indicate that A saucy sliver of toe and a beckoning, warped heel have become immediately identifiable Jude signatures. The Paris-based footwear label was founded in 2024 by Jurgita Dileviciute and Denitsa Bumbarova, and the duo’s subtly subversive designs take familiar shoe silhouettes and give them a deliciously peculiar twist—most notably with their barely-there peep toes. Zoë Kravitz is a fan of the Date pump, while Sarah Pidgeon favors the Date mule. Tracee Ellis Ross has amassed a well-curated collection of Jude footwear, from the sinuous Fame pump to the Haze sandal. It’s little wonder the label has found favor with fashion’s freakiest feet: Jude knows that even the smallest detail can demand a double take at the dogs.

Breaking: The Best Air Fryers For Faster, Crispier Cooking (2026)

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, buzzy as they’ve become over the past several years, air fryers are really just small ovens with fans built into them, i.e., convection ovens that circulate hot air around your food. Our years of testing air fryers (and we’ve used over two dozen in that time) have taught us that there are plenty out there that can give you crispy-enough results—but the very best air fryers churn out not only golden brown French fries and crispy-skinned chicken wings, but tender fillets of salmon and even whole roast chickens at the touch of a button.

Air fryers can take a few forms; the robot-esque basket-style models are probably what come to mind when you think of an air fryer, but there are versatile countertop convection ovens that add bake, broil, toast, and slow-cook options to the air fryer functionality. Some even dehydrate and steam too. And most recently, more bowl-style air fryers have started to hit shelves, which swap a slide-in basket for a glass container and top-down, air-frying lid.

The best for all varieties of air fryer needs are below.

According to recent reports, updated 11/23/26: There may not be a more popular Black Friday sale item than an air fryer. And all our favorites have discounts this week, including our overall top Cosori pick for less than $100. High-tech options from Breville, Cuisinart, Instant Pot, and Ninja are deeply discounted, too.

Clearview 4-Quart Glass Basket Air Fryer.

Vortex Plus 6-Quart ClearCook Air Fryer.

Ninja SL401 DoubleStack XL 2-Basket Air Fryer.

Instant Vortex Slim XL 6-Quart Air Fryer.

Most air fryers fit into one of three categories: oven, basket, or bowl.

A countertop convection oven, or air fryer–toaster oven, combines most of the crisping power of the basket-style air fryers you know and love with the multifunctionality you get from a toaster oven or countertop oven. Generally, the “air frying” function is achieved with a perforated slide-in rack, which usually means lots of cooking surface, but the racks are usually shallow and can require careful tossing or flipping of whatever you’re cooking, depending on the dish. But air fryer ovens, like the Breville Smart Oven Pro with its 13 different cooking modes, can do a lot, making them bona fide do-it-all kitchen appliances.

Basket-style air fryers aren’t as versatile as air fryer ovens, but they’re also less expensive and take up less space. They also tend to deliver better final results on traditional air fryer stuff like crisping up small foods that require shaking (tater tots, French fries, or Brussels sprouts), for which a handled basket is far easier to maneuver. Minuses are that they can be hard to clean and are limited in square inches inside the basket. They’re also sometimes made of plastic or nonstick-coated materials, which may not appeal to some consumers.

Bowl air fryers offer some of the best (and worst) of both worlds and also some unique benefits. Most of these include a heat-resistant glass bowl acting as the basket. Some models operate much like basket air fryers, with the glass container sliding into the base unit, while others opt for a “lid” that sits on top and houses the air frying mechanism. The glass baskets make these very easy to clean (included crisping trays are another story), however their functionality for shaking and pausing to flip foods can be cumbersome. But many come with lids for the glass containers, letting them double as prep and storage containers too.

Capacity: 6 qt.Wattage: 172510 Cooking functions: Air Fry, Roast, Broil, Frozen, Preheat, Reheat, Dehydrate, Proof, Bake, and Keep WarmColor: WhiteWeight: 11.5 lb.Dimensions: 11.8" x 14.4" x 11.9"Warranty: 2 years.

What we love: The 6-Quart Cosori Turboblaze Smart Air Fryer impressed us in every test, producing evenly browned and crispy frozen sweet potato fries, juicy chicken breasts, and perfectly cooked brussels sprouts. It has a straightforward digital interface that allows you to easily set the time and temperature and an impressive array of preset programs (Air Fry, Roast, Broil, Frozen, Preheat, Reheat, Dehydrate, Proof, Bake, and Keep Warm).

Recent findings suggest that A few things set the Turboblaze apart from the competition (including the previous longtime winner of this test, the Instant Vortex Slim). Most notably, it consistently produced the crispiest food of any air fryer we tested in record time. That may have something to do with the fact that there’s more space between the crisper plate (where the food sits) and the bottom of the basket than there is in some of the other top-performing models we’ve tried, which allows for better air circulation.

In a recent development, another standout feature is its variable fan speeds, which adjust automatically depending on the cooking function. Unlike most air fryers that use this tech behind the scenes, the Turboblaze demonstrates you the fan speed right on the display. Air Fry, for example, is one of four “turbo modes,” running the fan at full blast (speed 5), while Bake uses a gentler speed 3 to avoid disrupting delicate foods. Low-temperature settings like Dehydrate and Proof drop all the way down to speed 1.

It has been revealed that the Cosori Turboblaze is also a real value pick. The top performer in its price range (100–150) by a wide margin, it’s powerful, versatile, quiet, lightweight, and easy to clean (the brand notes both the nonstick basket and cooking tray are dishwasher-safe, though we recommend hand-washing anything with a nonstick coating).

According to recent reports, the model we tested includes smart features, meaning you can control it remotely or use voice commands via the VeSync app. If that’s not your thing, Cosori also sells a non-smart version for about $10 less.

Industry observers note that what we’d leave: Our gripes with this model are minor. It’s slightly annoying that you have to press a release button to pull the basket out. And while the greater amount of space between the crisper tray and basket bottom contributes to better airflow (and thus better browning), it means food is more likely to fall through while cooking.

Capacity: 2.1-qt.Wattage: 9004 cooking functions: Air-Fry, Bake, Roast, ReheatColors: Gray, red, white, greenWeight: 4.9 lb.Dimensions: 10.1" x 8.3" x 10.5"Warranty: 2 years.

If you’re on a tighter budget, have very little counter space to spare, or are mostly crisping up food just for yourself, consider the Cosori Lite 2.1-Quart Mini Air Fryer.

Recent findings suggest that what we love: This compact air fryer did a beautiful job crisping and browning small servings of frozen tater tots and fries, sliced zucchini, and veggie burger patties (two at a time, max). Depending on where you buy, it will only costs $50–$60 (as of publish time)—not at all bad for a lightweight, quiet, digital air fryer with four easy-to-use presets (air-fry, roast, bake, and reheat). It’s easy to tuck into a cabinet and to clean. Like the Cosori Blaze, the Lite has a nonstick basket. Again, while the manual claims the nonstick basket is dishwasher-safe, we always recommend hand-washing anything with a nonstick coating.

In a recent development, what we’d leave: Per its name, it’s quite small—don’t expect to be cooking enough food for more than two people in this thing. It also won’t remind you when it’s time to shake your food, so you’ll need to keep an eye on the timer yourself (luckily, the digital display makes this pretty easy).

Sources indicate that if you want an air fryer with maximum versatility and have some counter space to spare, spring for the Breville Smart Oven Air Fryer Pro. Breville makes a few different models (which can be found in the kitchens of many of our editors), but this one is the best combination of performance and value.

What we love: This midrange model has been our top pick for years now because of its versatility, build quality, intuitive design, and consistently strong performance in testing.

In testing, the Smart Oven Air Fryer Pro delivered reliably great results. It excelled at foods that need to be laid in a flat, even layer across the crisper tray (think veggie burgers or salmon fillets), but also handled frozen fries, tots, and sweet potato fries well. Its interior is roomy enough to fit a quarter sheet pan or 13x9" casserole pan, which means it can effectively double your oven space (or eliminate the need to turn on your full-size oven altogether).

This model is also a favorite among BA staffers and Test Kitchen editors, as well as award-winning cookbook author Nik Sharma, who developed some of BA’s favorite air fryer recipes. “I prefer toaster-oven-style to basket-style air fryers, because they’re easier to use for more common tasks like baking, toasting bread, and roasting more efficiently,” Sharma notes.

What we’d leave: As with most oven-style air fryers, it’s harder to toss or shake small foods mid-cook compared to a basket-style machine. We also found that, in general, food benefited from a higher cooking temperature (and often slightly longer cook time) relative to the basket-style winners.

Capacity: .5 cubic feetWattage: 18005 Cooking functions: Toast, Bagel, Broil, Pizza, Bake & Roast5 Air-frying functions: Air-Fry, Fries, Wings, Bacon, Crispy ReheatColor: Stainless steelWeight: 15.8 lb.Dimensions: 15.7" x 16.9" x 10"Warranty: 2 years.

If you like the idea of going the air fryer–toaster oven route but (1) don’t have the space for the Smart Oven Air Fryer Pro or (2) don’t want to shell out $400 in pursuit of crispiness, here’s some good news: Breville offers the Smart Oven Air Fryer Compact, which is essentially a smaller, cheaper version of our top pick.

What we love: As with most Breville products, the Smart Oven Air Fryer Compact feels thoughtfully designed, with stainless-steel finishes and a solid build. There are fewer niche modes than the Pro—no Dehydrate or Proof—but it does include four air-frying-specific presets in addition to a standard Air Fry setting.

We found using the Compact intuitive (the guide printed on the inside of the oven door helped). We also appreciated the “bit more” button, a feature borrowed from Breville’s toasters that adds a touch of extra cooking time when your fries are looking just a touch underdone.

According to recent reports, this model performed comparably to the Smart Oven Air Fryer Pro in most of our tests, producing juicy chicken, evenly browned cubes of tofu, and crispy veggies. We still prefer the larger model for its versatility and additional functionality, but this little oven would make a worthy addition to any smaller kitchen.

Industry observers note that what we’d leave: While the Compact did well in most tests, it struggled a bit with frozen sweet potato fries. This largely came down to overcrowding due to the smaller capacity: While we tried to fit an entire bag’s worth on a single tray, the unevenness with which the fries browned is a good example of the fact that, unlike a basket fryer, countertop oven-style air fryers are best used to cook things in a single layer.

Industry observers note that as mentioned, there’s a guide to oven inserts and placement on the inside of the oven’s door, but this is easy to miss, and these suggestions did not appear in full in the manual. Because of this, one tester accidentally cooked chicken with no tray underneath the wire basket to catch the drippings, which resulted in a smoking-hot mess.

It’s also worth noting that one of the major benefits of opting for an oven-style air fryer tends to be capacity, but the Compact wasn’t able to fit more food than our top basket-style pick.

The Breville Smart Oven Air Fryer Compact (L) is much smaller than the Smart Oven Air Fryer Pro (R).

Clearview 4-Quart Glass Basket Air Fryer.

According to recent reports, fresh on the market in 2026, Cuisinart’s ClearView series of air fryers truly delivers on its name with the introduction of a glass basket model that also sports a viewing window on the top of the unit (the line also features a larger, 9-qt. non-glass model). Unlike other glass air fryers we tried, this one operates more like the basket-style most people expect when they think of an air fryer.

In a recent development, what we love: The ClearView got high marks across the board in our tests comparing glass air fryers head-to-head, almost always offering up the winning results. The controls are easy to navigate, and the functions are intuitive with beeps to remind you to flip or shake your food when your cook is halfway through. In addition to the usual Air Fry, Bake, and Reheat functions, Cuisinart’s also offers a Keep Warm. Plus, there are two programmable custom presets if you’re cooking the same foods frequently.

Recent findings suggest that the crisper plate is nonstick, coated in PFAS-free ceramic, making it a breeze to clean with a little soap and water (or just throw it in the dishwasher). The glass basket is also dishwasher-safe. The ClearView doesn’t have any kind of mesh or grate covering the heating mechanism. We’ll continue to see how this fares over time, but in the meantime it’s nice not worrying about another greasy, perforated plate to clean. Lastly, the ClearView 4-Quart Glass Basket Air Fryer also comes in four colors—Black, Toasted Oat, Sage, and Tahini—and, as with all countertop appliances, it’s nice to have some kind of choice behind black plastic and stainless steel.

What we’d leave: The cord wrap post noticeably sticks out from the back of the unit. While this is probably great for airflow safety, it adds inches to a machine that’s also tall. And unlike some of the other glass air fryers we tried, Cuisinart’s bowl is oven or microwave safe. Granted, the point of the bowl is to air-fry, but if you’re using to carry your lunch into the office after cooking the night before, reheating is a little trickier.

We won’t go down the PFAS rabbit hole and get deep into the concept of “nontoxic” cookware right here and now (we've got other articles for that), but given the way the concept has come front and center we know some people want an air fryer with a PFAS-free nonstick basket—and for that, we recommend the Cosori Iconic.

What we love: It has similar features and produces similar results to our top pick, the Cosori TurboBlaze, churning out crispy-skinned salmon and beautifully browned Brussels. Like the TurboBlaze, the Iconic allows you to choose between five different fan speeds, which means it's equally adept at turning delicate kale into crispy chips without blowing them around the basket as it is cooking hefty bone-in chicken breasts to bronzed perfection.

And for those looking to eliminate PFAS from every inch of their kitchen, it has both a PFAS-free ceramic nonstick-coated basket and crisper plate.

What we’d leave: Aesthetically, it may not be for everyone as this stainless-steel air fryer looks a bit spaceship-like. But the real downside is the price, which is practically double that of the TurboBlaze.

Sources indicate that in the long run: The Cosori Iconic has seamlessly fit into the life of BA’s head of video, Dan Siegel. The speed is what won him over: “I shave 25% or more off any package-recommended cooking time and achieve perfect browning and crisping on every cook. The nonstick surfaces of both the basket and the included rack are remarkably easy to clean, making this my go-to appliance. My toaster oven probably misses me.” He mostly uses it for his two kids, occasionally scaling up to cook chicken breasts for his family of four, which takes two batches. (“It’s not huge.”) Despite the mirror-like stainless-steel finish, upkeep has been simple: “I haven't had any complications; I really only touch the top and the basket.” And then there’s the look. "It looks grown-up, like an actual appliance and not a major plastic toy without looking industrial. The MacBook of air fryers.".

According to recent reports, we have spent hours and hours over the past few years researching, testing, and retesting popular air fryers from top-name brands, including Breville, Cuisinart, Ninja, Philips, and Cosori. Here's how we put each appliance to the test:.

When evaluating each model, we looked for a few key qualities:.

4-Quart Vortex 6-in-1 Mini Air Fryer.

It has been revealed that this model from Instant Pot is a great option if a full-size (6-qt. or more) air fryer feels too big for your space or lifestyle, but our winning mini model (2-qt. limit) is too small. There’s a lot to love here, including the intuitive controls and presets, the viewing window and built-in light, and the ceramic nonstick interior coating. In testing, we found it did a decent job crisping everything we threw at it, though its performance didn’t quite match the winning Cosori Turboblaze.

Instant Vortex Slim XL 6-Quart Air Fryer.

Recent findings suggest that this model from Instant was a previous top pick, and we still think it’s an excellent air fryer. Its design, although compact, offers a significantly larger cooking surface area than comparably sized air fryers thanks to the shape of its basket. In practice, this meant our tester was able to fit an entire extra veggie burger patty (six total) compared to models of a similar size and generally cook more food in each batch without sacrificing any of the airflow that makes air-fried food so crispy.

Vortex Plus 6-Quart ClearCook Air Fryer.

It has been revealed that if a basket-style air fryer is what you’re after and you like the idea of being able to monitor what you’re cooking, the Instant Pot Vortex Plus ClearCook is definitely worth considering. This model performed nearly identically to our old top pick, the Instant Vortex Slim (probably because it’s a very similar build). The major difference—besides the ClearCook’s dimensions—is that it has a cooking window located at the front of its basket, plus a button that switches on an interior light, sort of like a traditional oven. This makes tracking the progress of your tots, fries, or chicken wings possible without removing the basket and disrupting the cooking process. Considering that providing a certain level of brownness is one of the chief concerns in air fryer cooking, this really comes in handy. A few more bonus points for the ClearCook: It adds Dehydrate to its list of functions and can hold temperatures as low as 95°F (the low end of the Vortex Slim’s range is 120°F). The ClearCook also happens to be $30 cheaper than the Slim at full price. On the downside, the square shape of the ClearCook’s basket fits one less veggie burger patty than more elongated baskets. It’s also a bit bulky.

Recent findings suggest that the Typhur Dome 2 is notably spacious compared to other basket-style fryers, with 139.5 square inches of cooking surface that fits a 12" pizza, 20 chicken wings, or 11 large chicken thighs per batch, and a digital panel with 15 presets plus a companion app offering more settings, self-cleaning, and one-touch recipes. We used to recommend the original Typhur Dome as a top pick for extra-large capacity, but after testing the Dome 2, which replaced it, we felt its performance didn’t quite merit a spot on our top picks: When filled to capacity, it took much longer to properly cook and crisp food than most other basket air fryers, and 11 bone-in chicken thighs took upward of 45 minutes to get truly golden, a major red flag given that cutting cooking time is a big reason to choose an air fryer over the oven. That said, the Dome 2 cooks food evenly and does eventually get very crisp, so if you’re feeding a large family and have counter space to spare, it may still be worth the investment.

According to recent reports, the Philips almost took a top spot—almost. It’s got a generous capacity, the control panel is easy to navigate, and it performs well with minimal user intervention. In other words, you won’t have to do a lot of shaking or stirring to get crispy fries from the Philips. This model did have a smaller yet heavier basket, and it’s loud and harder to clean due to a bunch of interlocking parts. It’s a good air fryer, but with its higher price tag, we feel like there are better deals on this list.

This newer model from Philips has a lot going for it: sleek touchscreen interface, helpful viewing window, and a whopping 16 settings. It did very well in our testing, producing crispy tots, tofu, and fries, but we preferred the design and the interface of the Cosori and Instant models. If you’re looking for an air fryer with a window feature, we’d recommend going with the Instant ClearCook (slightly cheaper at the time of writing) unless you find this model at a discount.

In a recent development, the Dreo ChefMaker isn't just an air fryer—it's also got probe cooking capabilities and app compatibility that make cooking proteins pretty effortless, and is a personal favorite of senior editor Olivia Tarantino. For the purposes of this article, though, we mainly tested its air frying abilities. We found that while the Dreo performed well, the winning TurboBlaze produced crispier, more evenly-cooked results all while ringing in at a third of the price. That noted, if the probe cooking feature intrigues you, this fryer might be worth a try.

It has been revealed that our Place partnered with James Beard Award–winning chef and cookbook author J. Kenji López-Alt on this updated version of the Wonder Oven, which features eight cooking functions, a touchscreen interface, and a roomy three-tier 30-liter capacity. Like all of Our Place's products, this little oven is an aesthete’s dream—but looks aside, it impressed us. It’s incredibly powerful, able to crisp brussels sprouts, tofu, and fries up to twice as fast as the winning Breville. It produced tender salmon with potato-chip-like skin in just seven minutes. Despite its smaller footprint, it’s large enough to fit a quarter-sheet pan, making it a good option if you want to save a few inches of counter space.

Industry observers note that all that noted, while the Wonder Oven Pro is generally well-designed, a few features were annoying to use. The touchscreen isn’t the most responsive. But the bigger glitch we had was with the preheating cycle. Preheating this oven to 400°F took 8–9 minutes from cold, which is already slower than the Breville’s 4–5. But more importantly, the Breville (like most regular ovens) takes less time to preheat when it’s already at temp. The Wonder Oven Pro, on the other hand, seemed to kick off a whole fresh several-minutes-long preheat cycle even when it had just been heated, only after which the timer would start.

Cuisinart Air Fryer Oven 6-Qt Basket Stainless Steel Air Fryer.

The Cuisinart was easy to use, didn’t whirr too loudly, included a nice preheat feature, and was about the same price. We also really liked the viewing window you could use to check the progress of your food. However, its deeper square-shaped basket has less surface area than something like the Instant Vortex Slim’s rectangular one, which limits its capacity.

Ninja SL401 DoubleStack XL 2-Basket Air Fryer.

The DoubleStack takes the idea of a dual-basket air fryer to a whole new level—literally. Like the Vortex Slim, the DoubleStack’s design prioritizes using vertical space. It’s skinny with the baskets stacked on top of each other instead of side by side like most other dual models. This makes it narrow and tall instead of wide, but not so tall that you can’t nestle it under your cabinets. Despite its space-saving design, you don’t lose out on actual cooking space. The baskets are substantial enough to fit a chicken, and the wire racks in each mean you can really maximize how much you’re cooking. (Though you do need to remain mindful of not overloading it with food, otherwise you’ll block the airflow and mess up the whole air-frying process.) You can also program the baskets separately and utilize the machine’s Smart Finish feature—which delays the start of the basket with the shorter cook—to have a whole meal ready at the same time. The one thing we didn’t like was the somewhat confusing interface.

AeroLucen 5-quart Glass Air Fryer.

It has been revealed that like the Cuisinart ClearView we recommend above, this glass air fryer operates like a traditional basket air fryer, in fact even more so as it features a front-mounted basket handle with slide-in operation. It’s a sleek-looking machine with a glossy top that illuminates when powered on with all of your touch-surface buttons. And we like that’s is relatively compact at just over 9.5" tall, making it great for in-cabinet storage. In the glass category, it performed nearly as well as the Cuisinart across the board with just a few cases of less even results, but we’re really nitpicking. What we didn’t like was the mesh-style crisping plate, which is tedious to clean and sits awkwardly on some jutting posts inside the basket, (though its design does offer a high and low position for maximizing space or airflow). That mesh is repeated on the underside of the heating element, something we don’t look forward to cleaning after a few dozen oil-evaporating cooking cycles. The internal light is intended to help you see what you’re cooking, but it glows red, which isn’t so helpful when you’re trying to keep an eye on browning.

Of the lid-style glass bowl air fryers we tested, this one was the easiest to maneuver with a fold-away handle that makes removing the top easy for flipping or shaking in the middle of cooking. With fine-tunable controls, it nailed crunchy skin on chicken thighs and crispy brussels sprouts with tender centers. More delicate dishes like salmon didn’t get where we wanted on the first try, and tofu cubes required more time than the recipe allotted to get anywhere near crispy enough. It fell short, as a lot of the glass bowl fryers did, on frozen fries, yielding uneven results and underdone portions when using the settings suggested on the back of the bag. We wish the “flip” alert was more than just a light, and it’s a little odd that the “Dehydrate” setting is listed as a bonus because you have to long-press another button to use it. The attached feet also mean the glass bowl can’t be put in the oven or microwave, but it is dishwasher-safe and comes with a lid. Plus, the whole fryer and basket setup is designed to nest inside itself for storage. And of this style of meal-prep-friendly air fryers, it’s the best version.

Instant Vortex Plus 4-Quart Air Fryer.

According to recent reports, this Instant Pot air fryer model is if you need something with a smaller capacity. The rectangular shape of its basket made it easy to fit plenty of food inside. It is sleek and has a short profile, which are nice features too. The Vortex Slim just offered better performance.

This is Ninja's basic basket air fryer. It’s lightweight and simple to use, and it does a nice job crisping up fries. The round shape of its basket, though, makes it less versatile than other models on this list. If you’re trying to cook raw proteins or a tray of vegetables, you give away a lot of space with a round basket.

In a recent development, while the Dash looks cute with its retro silhouette and poppy colors, it just didn’t perform that well. Sweet potato fries came out soggy and greasy. Tofu cubes got crisped on one side but were raw on the other, and the round basket could only fit one veggie burger. The two dials, controlling time and temperature, also prevented us from getting more specific in the cook settings.

Panasonic FlashXpress Air Fryer Toaster Oven.

Recent findings suggest that this oven-style air fryer from Panasonic performed well in our testing, but we found it frustrating to use for a few reasons. It has 12 different functions, but they come with very little on the display as to what each of these functions truly means. The Air Fry mode only allowed us to select temperatures between 410℉–445℉, which seemed quite high for certain foods. We also disliked the automatic preheating period that we couldn’t bypass even if the oven was already hot (this was particularly annoying when we just wanted to tack on an extra few minutes after finishing a cooking cycle). If you want to do that, you have to take the extra step of once again pressing the start button after the preheating process in order to start the timed cook cycle.

Like all of DTC darling Our Place’s products, the original Wonder Oven is cute. Unfortunately, it failed to impress us enough to earn a recommendation here. While it did fine at cooking tater tots and french fries, it produced unevenly browned, ultra mushy zucchini and tofu that never quite got the crisp exterior we were looking for. The analog controls are aesthetically pleasing, but make selecting an exact temperature impossible (and knowing when the unit is at temperature impossible too). It did, however, make a shockingly good fillet of crispy-skinned salmon.

It has been revealed that rather than a typical basket system, the Crispi consists of a glass container and a PowerPod that sits on top. The idea is that you can store your food directly in the glass containers, and Crispi sets include as many as three basket sizes (with more available). While most food did get crisp in the Crispi (you’d hope so with a name like that!), it took longer to do so than in a standard basket air fryer, and we found that food cooked somewhat unevenly. We tested this unit twice, the second time head-to-head with other glass air fryers, and our biggest gripe remains that there’s no precise temperature control—instead, you must choose between four preset modes (Max Crisp, Bake, Air Fry, and Recrisp). We thought that lack of precision made this model less versatile, and remembering which mode to use for which temperature number recommended on the bag of frozen fries or other foods wasn’t very user-friendly.

The Typhur Sync has lots of bells and whistles, like a wireless probe thermometer (with a built-in charging port), app compatibility, a PFAS-free basket, and nine total programs (including the three found only in the app). In testing, though, it failed to produce as impressive results as the winning Cosori. The fries browned, but many remained soggy, the salmon skin failed to crisp, and the Brussels sprouts didn’t quite get as golden as we’d have liked. While some of this might be solved by tinkering with time and temperature, at $160, we just didn’t feel this air fryer was worth the splurge.

In its defense, Magnifique’s Glass Air Fryer has some thoughtful features: two sizes of glass baskets (4.5-qt. and 2.5-qt.), each with lids, and a silicone base that’s easy to remove for cleaning and oven or microwave cooking (something Cuisinart and Ninja can’t match). It’s also the only glass air fryer we tested in this round that could possibly hold a small pizza with an 8.5" diameter crisper plate. However, there are more than a few aspects that weren’t as user-friendly. The stainless-steel crisper plate (no nonstick coating whatsoever) was the most difficult to clean by far, not only because of that lack of coating but because of the perforation pattern as well. The instructions specifically say don’t use scouring pads, but a gentle scrub with a plastic pad was the only way we could remove all the residue. There’s no reminder to flip or shake your food halfway through, a pretty standard-issue beep on many other units, and when you do take the lid off, you have to actually hit Start again to keep going, something other fryers do automatically. Results, especially with frozen foods like fries, were uneven, and fine-tuning is near impossible as its interface only allows for four preset cooking modes with no customization. If you’re following a recipe, you’ll have to remember which mode gets to which general temperature range and hope for the best.

In a recent development, what is an air fryer? Is it just a convection oven?

An air fryer is a countertop oven that uses hot air, circulated by a fan, to give foods crisper textures than you can achieve in a regular oven or toaster oven. What makes an air fryer a “fryer” is a built-in convection fan that blows the hot air around the food to crisp it up. It’s the combination of heat and moving air that produces the kind of crispy exterior you’d otherwise get from deep-frying or pan-frying. But unlike a deep fryer, an air fryer requires far less oil to achieve the desired effect—and it doesn’t leave your house smelling like a grease trap for days or weeks. So, technically speaking, yes, air fryers are just small convection ovens, but the most classic form of air fryer isn’t usually oven-shaped, rather more like egg or block with a slide-out basket on the front.

Recent findings suggest that whether you’re a purist and only consider products that contain baskets to be true air fryers, or you find the term air fryer to be stupid marketing jargon for a convection oven is up to you to decide. For the purposes of this review, we’ve included both toaster ovens that contain convection or “air fryer” settings and basket or bowl air fryers.

What accessories should I buy for my air fryer?

Recent findings suggest that there are a few extras you can buy to optimize your frying experience—things like an olive oil sprayer (so you can crisp without spilling oil on the heating element), parchment paper liners, and an instant read thermometer. For more of our favorite air fryer accessories, head right this way.

It has been revealed that alaina Chou: I’ve been testing air fryers and other small appliances for Bon Appétit and Epicurious since 2023. In that time, I’ve cooked countless batches of salmon, brussels sprouts, and frozen fries in pursuit of an air fryer that delivers on the lofty promise of deep-fryer-level crispiness without the need for a vat of hot oil. And I’ve blown out the power in the Test Kitchen numerous times in the process (sorry, Test Kitchen editors).

How Am I Supposed to Survive the Apocalypse Without My Phone?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that anyone who’s ever been trapped on a stalled subway or a WiFi-less flight knows how screwed we might feel without access to our phones.
  • It has been revealed that many found their way to Nomad, a pocket-sized device created to aid in offline situations.
  • Elsewhere, there are emergency libraries that you can download to your existing computer, with offline chatbots that can tell you how to find clean water or start a fire: lastbook.org, which includes how-to videos; Survival LLM, which offers up information from the CDC and FEMA; and Project Nomad (different from Studner’s Nomad), from Chris Sherwood, a prominent YouTuber.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that anyone who’s ever been trapped on a stalled subway or a WiFi-less flight knows how screwed we might feel without access to our phones. Last week’s tech outages––first, a failure of Microsoft’s systems, then, a national grounding of flights, followed by problems from Charles Schwab to Apple iCloud––were a reminder of how fragile our digital infrastructure is, especially at the dawn of AI. Preppers on Reddit, better known for discussing generators and the storage of food, began talking about how to AI–apocalypse proof the devices we’re all so dependent on. “getting serious about my preps with all the cyber attacks going on,” one user wrote. “I work for a security firm so I get a front row seat to a lot of the chaos. I’m specifically prepping for prolonged loss of power.”.

It has been revealed that many found their way to Nomad, a pocket-sized device created to aid in offline situations. “I had huge, huge spikes in traffic,” stated Jackson Studner, creator of Nomad and a student at Millersville University of Pennsylvania. (“I’m not a tech giant or a startup, just a college student who enjoys building useful things and sharing them,” Studner’s website reads.) With the help of his professors, he built Nomad to provide some entertainment on camping trips and cross-country trips with friends. They’d hit a dead zone, and realize they wanted to watch a movie, or run video game software. Nomad is a miniscule server with TV and films, the entire Wikipedia library, and portable Wi-Fi, and offline maps. “I really like the reliability aspect,” Studner tells me. “I like to own my stuff. It's kind of that simple.” He’s also added navigation for his latest community preparing for the apocalypse (or at least a grid shutdown). “It will actually tell you how to go along the road, it can tell you how to walk there, it'll calculate times, that kind of stuff,” he said.

Elsewhere, there are emergency libraries that you can download to your existing computer, with offline chatbots that can tell you how to find clean water or start a fire: lastbook.org, which includes how-to videos; Survival LLM, which offers up information from the CDC and FEMA; and Project Nomad (different from Studner’s Nomad), from Chris Sherwood, a prominent YouTuber. Sherwood is best known for posting explainer videos showing viewers how to build their “homelabs”—personal, at-home computing devices—under the name Crosstalk Solutions.

The interest in Project Nomad, Sherwood stated, has been overwhelming. “It’s got over 40,000 stars on GitHub, which means that 40,000 people not only saw the project and were on the page, but they clicked the little button to favorite it. And I'm getting over 200,000 views on the website per month,” he said.

Industry observers note that despite his latest fans, Sherwood himself isn’t a prepper. He was inspired by the Information Technology Disaster Resource Center (ITDRC), a non-profit that goes into disasters and provides internet services when they are completely down. “I had the opportunity to go on deployment with [ITDRC] when Hurricane Ian came through, and I saw firsthand all these people that were offline. It was a disaster. Getting people back online was almost as important as the food and water supplies that were getting set up to help with the recovery,” he explained.

Recent findings suggest that studner wasn’t a prepper either–– at first. But since Nomad took off and he’s found himself in more “prepper” corners of the internet, his feelings have slightly changed. “It’s for peace of mind. I have my little go bag. I'm not too, too worried about it, but I like to know that if there ever was a real problem, I'd be okay in that situation.”.
